# iTrack Wave 3 — Design system and shell — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Land the approved "professional's ledger" identity as a token system, self-hosted type, a component library (Button, Modal/Sheet, Form primitives, Toast, EmptyState, PageHeader, Rail/BottomNav, ErrorBoundary) and the four instruments (CycleRing, DeadlineTimeline, CreditBar, StatusPill), replace the iOS push-stack shell with a persistent rail / bottom-nav shell on ordinary URL-per-screen routing, restyle the error and not-found routes, and gate the wave on the contrast audit (zero literals outside `app/styles/tokens.css`), axe on every route in all four Playwright projects (zero serious/critical), and committed desktop + phone screenshots in both schemes — without redesigning a single screen's content (that is Wave 4).

**Architecture:** `app/globals.css` is split first, mechanically and at pixel parity, into `app/styles/tokens.css` (the only token file: `:root {` first, one dark remap, then a `var()`-only LEGACY ALIAS block that maps every pre-Wave-3 token name onto the new palette so `app/ITrackApp.tsx` keeps rendering) plus per-screen consumer stylesheets (`home`, `credentials`, `credential-detail`, `log-activity`, `history`, `account`, `legacy-shared`) and new consumer files the primitives own (`fonts`, `primitives`, `instruments`, `shell`); `globals.css` shrinks to the imports plus an explicit reset (Tailwind and its preflight are removed). The screens stay inside `app/ITrackApp.tsx` this wave: only the shell (`AppShell` → `Rail`/`BottomNav`/`PageHeader`, `useNavigation` with `pushState`/`replaceState`/`popstate` and no depth or origin-tab state), the primitives under `app/components/`, the instruments under `app/components/instruments/` with their pure geometry in `app/lib/instruments.ts`, and the minimal in-place swaps the code maps name (hero ring/bar/pill, ProgressRow bar, check-in dot, the timeline card, ModalError → ErrorSummary, the personal-task editor and the template chooser on the Form primitives) touch `ITrackApp.tsx`. Every new stylesheet is a consumer that may not reference a legacy alias, every new component is proven on a dev-only `/styleguide` route as well as on the real screens, and every task rewrites the tests its change breaks in the same commit (pins are deleted whole, behaviour is asserted in `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` on the four projects or in `tests/*.test.mjs` against `.test-build/`).

**Tech Stack:** Node 22 (`node:test`, `node:sqlite` behind `--experimental-sqlite`), Vinext 0.0.50 / Next App Router on workerd via wrangler 4.92, React 19.2 (`createPortal`, `useId`, `useSyncExternalStore`-free), TypeScript 5.9 (`tsc --outDir .test-build --module nodenext` for pure-module tests), plain CSS with `@import` (Tailwind 4.2.1 and `@tailwindcss/postcss` removed this wave), self-hosted woff2 subsets built with fontTools 4.65 + brotli in a project-local venv (`tools/fonts/build-fonts.sh`), Playwright 1.63 (`@playwright/test`, four Chromium projects — scheme × viewport) plus **one new devDependency, `@axe-core/playwright` 4.13.0** (exact), Docker, Railway CLI 5.26.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-itrack-web-redesign-design.md` — this plan implements **section 5** (Wave 3 — Design system and shell: §5.1 identity — palette, type, instruments, motion, layout — and §5.2 primitives), the Wave 3 row of the **section 2** table (ships: tokens, type, primitives, app shell + navigation, error/not-found routes; finish gate: contrast audit green, both schemes, desktop + phone screenshots) and the Wave 3 lines of **section 9** (axe on every route with zero serious/critical violations is a gate from Wave 3; `tools/contrast-audit.mjs` across all stylesheets with zero literals outside token files; Playwright per screen, both colour schemes, 1440×900 and 390×844; Docker run-check before merge; live smoke after deploy). Sections 6 and 7 are Waves 4 and 5 and are deliberately not planned here — screen content, copy, the packet, the public funnel and the gateway pages stay as they are. The **approved mockup (direction A)** and the six decisions taken with the approval are `docs/design/2026-09-10-mockup-a/README.md` with the artboards `home-desktop.html` and `home-phone.html`; where the mockup and the spec disagree the spec wins (rem scale over the mockup's 11 px / 15 px / 40 px; nav labels Home / Credentials / Activity log / Account with the URL contract unchanged). Audit finding ids cited per task refer to `docs/audits/2026-09-10-audit/findings.json`; the eight verified code maps that accompany this plan are the source for every line number below (main @ `4bc32b5`, Waves 1 and 2 live on https://itrackceu.com).
## Global Constraints

- **Node:** use Node 22 at `$HOME/.local/node/node-v22.22.0-darwin-arm64/bin` (Node 25 on this machine has an npm/TLS bug). Every shell in this plan starts with `export PATH="$HOME/.local/node/node-v22.22.0-darwin-arm64/bin:$PATH"`.
- **Repo / branch:** `/Users/chrisskerritt/Documents/New project/Vigilo`, remote `origin` = `https://github.com/cskerritt/iTrack.git`. Work on branch `feat/wave3-design-system` cut from `main` at `4bc32b5` (Waves 1 and 2 merged and live) in the worktree `/Users/chrisskerritt/Documents/New project/Vigilo-wt/wave3` (`git worktree add "../Vigilo-wt/wave3" -b feat/wave3-design-system 4bc32b5` from the main checkout, then `npm ci` there — the main checkout's `node_modules` is stale and has no `@playwright/test`). Merge to `main` only in Task 15 (pushes to `main` auto-deploy to Railway). Run `git branch --show-current` before every commit — another session may share the main tree, and the `Vigilo-wt/wave2` worktree still exists (it is removed only after Chris confirms the Wave 2 browser checks; never touch it).
- **Dev server / ports:** `:3000` is often held by an unrelated `next-server` (mvqs-online); the Wave 3 dev server runs on **3100** and every Playwright command is prefixed `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100` (`playwright.config.ts` derives the port, the readiness URL and the `npm run dev -- --port 3100` command from it; `reuseExistingServer: true` would otherwise "reuse" the foreign server). Start it with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 npm run dev -- --port 3100 > "$HOME/Desktop/wave3-dev.log" 2>&1 &` and stop it with `kill "$(lsof -t -nP -iTCP:3100 -sTCP:LISTEN)"`. **Stop the :3100 dev server before `npm run build` / `npm test`** (they share `.wrangler/` state and the build clobbers it); start it again for Playwright.
- **Test entry points:** `npm test` = `npm run build && npm run build:lib-test && node --experimental-sqlite --test tests/*.test.mjs`. A full worker build takes minutes: while iterating run only your file, `node --experimental-sqlite --test tests/<file>.test.mjs` (after `npm run build:lib-test` for anything that imports `.test-build/`). Tests that import `dist/server/index.js` (`tests/rendered-html.test.mjs`, `tests/real-sqlite-seed.test.mjs`, `tests/isolation.test.mjs`, `tests/workspace-credential-actions.test.mjs`, `tests/workspace-cycles.test.mjs`) and `tests/dist-hygiene.test.mjs`'s dist assertions need `npm run build` first. `npm run test:e2e` (all four projects), `npm run test:e2e:desktop` and `npm run test:e2e:phone` are separate scripts and are never chained into `npm test`. `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`, which also typechecks `tests/e2e/*.ts`, `tests/live/*.ts` and `playwright.live.config.ts`) and `npm run lint` (`eslint .`, which lints `tests/` and runs eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7 — `refs`, `purity`, `set-state-in-effect`, `set-state-in-render` at error) are safe at any time. `node tools/contrast-audit.mjs` is build-free and must exit 0 at every commit. The unauthenticated Playwright live smoke (Task 15: `tests/live/live-smoke.spec.ts` under its own `playwright.live.config.ts`, `LIVE_BASE_URL=<origin>` required, no `webServer`, one desktop project) runs only against a gateway — the Docker run-check container or production — never against the dev server (which has no gateway) and never inside `npm run test:e2e` (its `testDir` is `tests/live`, outside the four-project suite).
- **Green at every commit:** each task rewrites the tests its change breaks in the same commit; `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `node tools/contrast-audit.mjs` must pass at every task's final step, and every task that touches `app/` or `tests/e2e/` also runs `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 npm run test:e2e` with the dev server up (all four projects green; `screenshots.spec.ts` and `parity.spec.ts` are the only specs allowed to report `skipped`, and only when their env var is unset).
- **Pins are deleted, never edited (ios-coupling-15):** a source-regex assertion is removed whole (with its `readFile` binding) or its whole subtest is removed; no regex is re-pointed at moved code. No file under `tests/` may read `app/ITrackApp.tsx`, `app/globals.css`, `app/layout.tsx`, `app/styles/*` or `app/components/*` as text, except the generic walkers in `tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs`, `tests/protected-identifiers.test.mjs` and the `tools/contrast-audit.mjs` importer in `tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs`; Task 9 extends the `no test file reads client source text` guard to `app/styles/` and `app/components/`. Server-source pins (`runtimeSource`, `workspaceRouteSource`, … over `public/sw.js`, `pushDeliverySource`, `wranglerSource`) stay this wave.
- **E2E identity rule:** the demo identity (`demo@local.license-lantern`, seeded by `ensureDemoWorkspace`) is read-only in every spec; any spec that saves anything uses `test.use({ identity: freshIdentity() })` from `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` and seeds through `/api/workspace`. Specs never put `userId`, `user_id`, `ownerId` or `owner_id` in a payload (400 `client_identity_forbidden`). Every new spec runs in all four projects unless its header says why not.
- **Keep-list (ios-coupling-10) — nothing in this wave edits:** `public/sw.js` (its precache list included — fonts are HTTP-cached, not service-worker-cached), `public/*.png`, `public/favicon.ico`; `app/lib/webPush.ts`, `app/lib/rfc8291Push.ts`, `app/lib/pushDelivery.ts`; the service-worker registration and the "Add iTrack to your phone" install-help sheet in `ITrackApp.tsx` (its `<Modal>` import swaps with every other site in Task 6 and nothing else changes); all `env(safe-area-inset-*)` uses (moved verbatim with their rules, never dropped) and the 16px iOS zoom floor (`input, select, textarea { font-size: max(var(--text-control), 1em); }` stays in `globals.css` and `--text-control` stays `16px`); the four route pages (`app/page.tsx`, `credentials/page.tsx`, `history/page.tsx`, `profile/page.tsx`, `credentials/[credentialId]/page.tsx` — comment-only edits in Task 9); `deploy/railway/pages/*.html` (their `:root` mirrors keep the OLD palette until Wave 5 and keep passing the audit as token files with 0 claims); `VAPID_*` and every other Railway variable; the seven protected identifiers (`tests/protected-identifiers.test.mjs`). **Wave 3 deliberately edits these Wave 2 keep-list items and nothing else on that list:** `app/layout.tsx` viewport theme colours (Task 1) and `RootLayout` head/body (Tasks 4, 8); `app/manifest.ts` colours (Task 1); `public/offline.html` metas + inline token mirror (Task 1); `.sheet-grabber` / `useSheetDragDismiss` / `useEdgeSwipeBack` / press and screen tokens (removed, Tasks 1, 2, 6, 9); `app/lib/navigation.ts` (the NavEntry half is deleted, Task 9).
- **URL contract unchanged:** `/`, `/credentials`, `/credentials/:id`, `/history`, `/profile` — `parseRoute`/`buildPath`/`isTabName` in `app/lib/navigation.ts` are kept verbatim. Only the labels change (Home / Credentials / Activity log / Account, phone label "Activity"; titles "Activity log · iTrack" / "Account · iTrack").
- **No screen content redesign (mockup README decision 1):** Home, Credentials, Credential detail, Log activity, Activity log, Account and the packet keep their markup and copy inside `app/ITrackApp.tsx`, rendering on the new tokens through the LEGACY ALIAS block of `app/styles/tokens.css`. The only `ITrackApp.tsx` edits are: the `<Modal>` / Icon / Button / Toast / PageHeader / EmptyState import swaps, the shell render tree, the navigation call sites, and the in-place swaps each task's brief names (hero ring / credits bar / status pill, ProgressRow bar, check-in dot, the "Next twelve months" timeline card, ModalError → ErrorSummary, `PersonalTaskEditorModal` and the template chooser on the Form primitives, the a11y-12 `role` additions). Nothing else moves, is renamed or is restyled. The Home two-column ledger (`minmax(0, 1fr) 380px`, 28 px gap — spec §5.1 Layout, mockup README "Desktop shell") is Home's own layout and lands in Wave 4 with the Home extraction; until then Task 11 mounts the "Next twelve months" timeline card full-width under the hero, and Task 1 declares the column's width as `--ledger-aside-width` (380px) so Wave 4 consumes a token, not a literal. The Wave 3 screenshots therefore show a single content column where the desktop artboard shows the ledger — that is decision 1, not drift.
- **Colour literals:** no hex, `rgb()`/`rgba()` without `var(--`, named colour or system colour may appear outside the first `:root {` block and the first `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block of `app/styles/tokens.css` (system colour keywords only inside a file's own `@media (forced-colors: active)` block) — `tools/contrast-audit.mjs` enforces it across `app/**/*.css` and the five gateway pages; `public/offline.html` and `app/layout.tsx`/`app/manifest.ts` are the only hand-mirrored literals and Task 1 lists their exact values. TSX carries no colour literal either (SVG `stroke`/`fill` come from CSS classes).
- **Type sizes:** every `font-size` under `app/**/*.css` is a `var(--text-*)` token or a `rem`/`%`/`em` value; the single px is `--text-control: 16px`, declared once in `tokens.css` (`tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs` enforces it from Task 2). The nine-step rem scale is `--text-2xs 0.75` · `--text-xs 0.8125` · `--text-sm 0.875` · `--text-md 1` (body) · `--text-lg 1.125` · `--text-xl 1.375` · `--text-2xl 1.75` · `--text-3xl 2.25` · `--text-4xl 3`; nothing declares a size below `--text-2xs` (the old 10px tab-label exception is retired — the bottom-nav label is `--text-2xs` on a 22px icon).
- **Legacy aliases are banned in new code:** every token name inside the `LEGACY ALIASES` block of `tokens.css` may be referenced only by `app/styles/legacy-shared.css`, `home.css`, `credentials.css`, `credential-detail.css`, `log-activity.css`, `history.css`, `account.css` and (until Task 2) `globals.css`. `app/styles/fonts.css`, `primitives.css`, `instruments.css`, `shell.css` and every new component reference only first-class tokens (`tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs` enforces it from Task 1). Wave 4 deletes the alias block with the last extracted screen.
- **Fonts:** three faces only — Bricolage Grotesque (display, 700/800), Atkinson Hyperlegible (body, 400/700/400 italic), "iTrack Mono" (IBM Plex Mono renamed for its Reserved Font Name, 400/500) — as latin-subset woff2 files under `public/fonts/` with content-hashed names, each ≤ 40 × 1024 bytes, `font-display: swap`, metric-matched `local()` fallbacks, the four first-paint faces preloaded from `app/layout.tsx`. No `next/font` (it recreates the `.vinext/fonts` cache that `tests/dist-hygiene.test.mjs` forbids), no request to `fonts.googleapis.com` / `fonts.gstatic.com` from the app, no `font-optical-sizing`/`font-variation-settings` (the shipped faces are static instances).
- **Motion:** exactly the three spec moments — a credit bar filling to its new value (400 ms ease-out), a ring segment completing plus the check drawing (400 ms arc, then a 320 ms check), and (Wave 4) a card folding to the ledger row — expressed through `--duration-fill` (the bar fill and the arc), `--duration-complete` (the check), `--duration-fold`, `--ease-out` in `tokens.css`, zeroed under `prefers-reduced-motion`; no duration literal appears outside `tokens.css`. Screen push/pop, sheet slide, scrim fade, press scale, hover lift and the edge-swipe/drag-dismiss gestures are removed (mockup README decision 6), never restyled. No transition or animation may be added to the shell or the primitives except the Button pending spinner.
- **Accessibility gates:** every route (`/`, `/credentials`, `/credentials/:id`, `/history`, `/profile`, `/nonexistent`, `/styleguide`) plus the Log activity sheet and the workspace-load-failure state pass axe with zero `serious`/`critical` violations in all four Playwright projects (Task 13, then at every later commit); one focus ring (`3px solid var(--focus-ring)`, offset 2px) on every focusable thing including form fields; `role="progressbar"` with numeric `aria-valuenow` on every ring and bar; dialogs keep their exact accessible names ("Log completed learning", "Set up a credential", "Log your submission", "Due-date check-ins", "Add a personal task", "Edit learning record", "Edit credential", "Delete <name>?", "Add iTrack to your phone"); the hydration placeholder keeps `aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading iTrack"` (every spec's `goto` waits on it); both navs keep `aria-label="Primary navigation"` and are server-rendered.
- **Modal render sites keep their shape:** every `<Modal>` site in `ITrackApp.tsx` stays spelled `{cond ? (\n<Modal` / `<…Modal` (the `handleSessionEnded` guard in `tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs` counts them: ≥ 6 gated, ≥ 5 ungated); the `/styleguide` route mounts its samples as `{open && <Modal …>}` so the guard does not count them.
- **Copy rules:** no "beta", no "Pro", no prices, no "ad-supported", no tiers anywhere (spec §1.3). New user-facing strings are exactly the ones written in each task's brief — Wave 4 rewrites copy, so add no other prose (the rail note "Rules come from the issuing body's published requirements, with a source link and review date on every template. The board's current instructions control.", the timeline card "Next twelve months" / "today" / "<names> sit beyond this window.", the pill words "Overdue" / "Due soon" / "On track" / "Submitted" / "Renewed" / "No cycle" / "Due today", the breadcrumb "Credentials", the error disclosure "Technical details", the styleguide's sample strings). No new string mentions Capacitor, TestFlight, "the shell", or native apps.
- **Dates:** no file under `app/` computes today in UTC (`new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, `const todayIso`); the timeline's `today` is the app's `today()` (`todayLocal(dateZone)`) passed down as a prop; every pure module added to `app/lib/` (`fonts.ts`, `modalStack.ts`, `selectFilter.ts`, `toastQueue.ts`, `instruments.ts`, `buttonClass.ts`) has no DOM/React/D1 import, uses the `./x.js` import suffix, and is appended to the `build:lib-test` tsc list in the task that creates it; clock reads stay in module-level helpers, never inside a component render (`react-hooks/purity`).
- **Migrations / identity:** none this wave (journal stays at idx 14 `0014_credential_archive`; no identity change, spec §8). `package.json` changes exactly three times: Task 3 removes `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/postcss` (`npm uninstall`, lockfile committed), Task 13 adds `@axe-core/playwright@4.13.0` (`npm install --save-dev --save-exact`, lockfile committed), and `build:lib-test` gains one file per pure module; nothing else in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` moves.
- **Protected identifiers (do not touch):** the `license-lantern:` hash salt (`db/identity.ts:49`), the demo email `demo@local.license-lantern` (`db/identity.ts:16`), the draft prefix `license-lantern:activity-draft:v1:` (`app/lib/activityDraft.ts:39,48`, `route.ts:427`), the ICS UID domain `@license-lantern` (`app/lib/calendarInvite.ts:143`), the push topic `license-lantern-check-in` (`app/lib/pushDelivery.ts:69`, `public/sw.js:159`), the SW cache prefix `license-lantern-static` (`public/sw.js:4`), the R2 bucket `vigilo-r2` (`vite.config.ts:35`), the `oai-authenticated-user-*` header names, the `itrack_session` cookie name. The `lantern-spin` keyframe is explicitly renameable and Task 12 renames it to `spin`.

### Task 1: The ledger palette lands: `app/styles/tokens.css` (85 audited claims) with the LEGACY ALIAS block, theme colours / manifest / offline page mirrored, contrast gate re-pointed, mockup approval committed

**Rationale:** spec §5.2 closes with the sentence this task implements — "Tokens in `app/styles/tokens.css`; per-screen styles in `app/styles/<screen>.css`; `globals.css` shrinks to resets + tokens import" — and the §2 table's Wave 3 row ships "tokens, type" first and gates the wave on "contrast audit green, both schemes". Every later Wave 3 task consumes these token names (the fonts in Task 4, the primitives in 5–8, the shell in 9, the instruments in 10–11, the error surfaces in 12), so the palette lands first and alone, and it lands everywhere at once: mockup README decision 1 keeps every screen inside `app/ITrackApp.tsx` on its 144 legacy token names, so the new file ends with a `var()`-only LEGACY ALIASES `:root` that maps each of them onto the new palette. This is architecture-11's advice ("do the split as one mechanical commit before any restyle") applied one level up — the colour flip is one commit whose proof is the audit tool's own numbers, before any rule moves (Task 2) or any component is written. The values are spec §5.1's light and dark palettes verbatim plus the three the approved mockup fixes (`docs/design/2026-09-10-mockup-a/README.md`: accent hover `#1B2F86`, the due-soon row edge `#E5C98A`, the inverse "Best next action" surface `#1C1A17` with paper text and muted `#C9C2B4`); the type scale is §5.1's nine `rem` steps (a11y-14: today `app/globals.css:52-57` is `12px … 17px` with no root size); the three font families are named now so Task 4's `@font-face` blocks bind to them (perf-08 — names only: no file, no request, the fallbacks render until Task 4). Two audit findings close inside this file: a11y-05 (the text-input boundary `--line-strong` on `--white` measures 1.58:1 light / 1.29:1 dark at `app/globals.css:20,381`) — `--line-strong` becomes a 3.9:1 / 3.5:1 boundary on `--card`, and the legacy `.field input, .field select { border: 1px solid var(--line-strong) }` rule (`:4094-4104`) inherits it through the alias with no CSS edit — and a11y-06 (`outline: none` plus a 0.13-alpha `--focus-glow` at `:4102,4110-4113`) — one `--focus-ring`, the accent in both schemes, painted by the reset's `:focus-visible` rule at 3px with a 2px offset; the glow tokens survive only as aliases. The hand-mirrored copies of the palette that architecture-13 names — `app/layout.tsx` `themeColor` (`:84-87`), `app/manifest.ts` (`:17-18`), `public/offline.html` (metas `:12,17` and its inline `:root` `:34-67`) — move in the same commit; the five `deploy/railway/pages/*.html` mirrors stay (Wave 5 rebuilds them; they remain token files with 0 claims and keep passing). The gate (spec §9 "Contrast: `tools/contrast-audit.mjs` across all stylesheets, zero literals outside token files") is re-pointed here: the tool needs no code change — `collectStylesheets` already walks `app/**/*.css` recursively, a `.css` whose first rule after leading `@import`/`@charset` is `:root {` is a token file, everything else is a consumer — so `tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs` is rewritten to pin `app/styles/tokens.css` as the ONLY token file under `app/`, every other app stylesheet as a literal-free consumer, and (new) no new stylesheet referencing a legacy alias. `docs/design/2026-09-10-mockup-a/` is untracked in git today (`?? docs/design/`); it enters history with this commit so the mockup gate the §2 table names ("Chris approves mockup") is on record.

**Decisions taken here (binding for every later task; where the code maps disagreed, this is the ruling):**

1. Semantic state tokens are named `--state-<name>` (ink) and `--state-<name>-soft` (fill) — not `--state-<name>-ink`, not `--overdue` / `--danger-soft`. The instruments' trough, minimum marker and axis are `--track`, `--marker` and `--line` (not `--instrument-*`); the toast's action colour on the inverse card is `--accent-on-inverse` (not `--on-inverse-accent`).
2. The text-input boundary (a11y-05) is `--line-strong` (light `#847f74` = 3.9:1 on `--card`, 3.6:1 on `--paper`; dark `#78725f` = 3.5:1 on `--card`, 3.9:1 on `--paper`). There is no `--edge-field`. Its name starts with `line`, so `tools/contrast-audit.mjs` `floorFor` holds it to the 3:1 object floor.
3. One focus ring: `--focus-ring` is the accent in both schemes; `--focus-glow`, `--focus-glow-strong`, `--focus-ring-soft`, `--edge-focus` and `--focus-ring-danger` survive only as aliases.
4. The six legacy type-scale names keep their names and become `rem`. `--text-2xs` 12px → 0.75rem, `--text-xs` 13px → 0.8125rem and `--text-sm` 14px → 0.875rem are exact at the 16px default; `--text-md` 15px → 1rem (16px) and `--text-lg` 17px → 1.125rem (18px) are NOT 1:1 — body copy grows one pixel this wave, because the spec's rem scale wins over the mockup's 15px (README: "where the mockup and the spec disagree the spec wins"). `--text-control` stays `16px` — the one px in the system, declared exactly once, consumed by the unchanged zoom-floor rule `input, select, textarea { font-size: max(var(--text-control), 1em); }`.
5. `theme-color` and the manifest's `theme_color` are paper-deep (`#ebe7dc` light, `#0f0e0b` dark): in mockup A the phone app bar sits directly under the status bar, so the chrome colour is the bar's colour, not the page's — the same argument the current `layout.tsx` comment makes for `--paper`. The manifest's `background_color` is paper (`#f5f2ea`): the splash is the page.
6. Dark elevation: spec dark paper `#15130f` → card `#1f1c16` measures 1.09:1 with the tool's formula (light paper → card is 1.10:1), under the old 1.15:1 dark-elevation convention in `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`. Spec wins; cards separate by the `--line` hairline (dark `--line` on `--card` is 1.28:1) and a 12px radius. Task 14 documents it; no token is nudged and no elevation claim is written.
7. Font family names are fixed now even though the files land in Task 4: display `"Bricolage Grotesque"`, body `"Atkinson Hyperlegible"`, mono `"iTrack Mono"` (IBM Plex Mono carries the Reserved Font Name "Plex"; a latin subset is a Modified Version and is renamed in Task 4), each followed by a `"… Fallback"` face Task 4 declares as a metric-matched `local()` font.
8. The graphite inverse family (`--ink-surface*`, `--on-dark*`, `--accent-bright`) is aliased as ONE unit onto `--inverse-surface` / `--on-inverse(-muted)` / `--accent-on-inverse`, which is ink in light and paper in dark — the legacy hero, sidebar and toast text stays readable in both schemes. (Task 11 flips the Home hero to a card surface with scoped overrides when the instruments land.)
9. The reset rules that stay in `globals.css` are rewritten onto first-class tokens now (body flat `--paper`, `--font-body`, `::selection` on `--accent-soft`, `:focus-visible` offset 2px, `.skip-link` on `--card`), so `globals.css` can join the alias guard in Task 2 with nothing left to change in the reset.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing gate — `tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs` rewritten whole, and the two rendered-output pins re-pointed**

Replace the whole of `tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs` with the file below. The first three tests describe the tree this task produces (one token file at `app/styles/tokens.css`, `globals.css` a consumer, an alias block no new stylesheet touches); the last two are the current file's tests 3 and 4 verbatim. Reading `tokens.css` as text inside `legacyAliasNames()` is the one sanctioned source read (Global Constraints: this file is the `tools/contrast-audit.mjs` importer), and the path is built from `root`, so it does not match the `../app/(ITrackApp.tsx|globals.css|layout.tsx)` regex in `tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs:153`.

```js
// Gate for the design-system contrast invariant (spec §9 "Contrast"): every
// stylesheet under app/ and every public page's <style> blocks pass
// tools/contrast-audit.mjs — each documented claim holds, and no colour
// literal sits outside a token file's token blocks. After Wave 3 the ONLY
// token file under app/ is app/styles/tokens.css; every other stylesheet
// under app/ is a consumer with zero literals, and a new stylesheet may not
// even reference a legacy alias. The tool is run exactly as a person runs
// it, so the exit code and the report lines are what is pinned. Build-free:
// `node --test tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs`.
import test from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { auditStylesheet, collectStylesheets, tokenBlocks } from "../tools/contrast-audit.mjs";

const root = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const PAGES = ["landing", "login", "signup", "verify", "reset"];
const TOKEN_FILE = "app/styles/tokens.css";
// The stylesheets ITrackApp.tsx's un-extracted screens still render on. They
// may reference the LEGACY ALIASES block; Wave 4 deletes them with it.
// Everything else under app/ is new code and may not.
const LEGACY_STYLESHEETS = new Set([
  "app/styles/legacy-shared.css",
  "app/styles/home.css",
  "app/styles/credentials.css",
  "app/styles/credential-detail.css",
  "app/styles/log-activity.css",
  "app/styles/history.css",
  "app/styles/account.css",
  // Task 2 removes this entry once globals.css is down to imports + resets.
  "app/globals.css",
]);
const escapeRegExp = (text) => text.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");

const runAudit = (...args) =>
  spawnSync(process.execPath, ["tools/contrast-audit.mjs", ...args], { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8" });

const appSheets = () => collectStylesheets(root).filter((sheet) => sheet.path.startsWith("app/"));

// Every `--name:` declared after the LEGACY ALIASES banner of tokens.css. The
// block is the last thing in the file, so everything after the banner is an
// alias declaration or a comment; the tool never reads claims from it.
function legacyAliasNames() {
  const css = readFileSync(path.join(root, TOKEN_FILE), "utf8");
  const start = css.indexOf("LEGACY ALIASES");
  assert.ok(start > 0, "tokens.css carries the LEGACY ALIASES banner");
  return [...css.slice(start).matchAll(/(--[a-z0-9-]+)\s*:/g)].map((match) => match[1]);
}

test("every stylesheet and public page passes the contrast audit", () => {
  const run = runAudit();
  assert.equal(run.status, 0, run.stdout + run.stderr);
  assert.match(run.stdout, /^contrast-audit: app\/styles\/tokens\.css — \d+ claims, 0 failing, 0 literals$/m);
  for (const sheet of appSheets()) {
    if (sheet.path === TOKEN_FILE) continue;
    assert.match(
      run.stdout,
      new RegExp(`^contrast-audit: ${escapeRegExp(sheet.path)} — 0 claims, 0 failing, 0 literals$`, "m"),
      `${sheet.path} is a consumer: no claims, no literals`,
    );
  }
  for (const page of PAGES) {
    assert.match(
      run.stdout,
      new RegExp(`^contrast-audit: deploy/railway/pages/${page}\\.html — 0 claims, 0 failing, 0 literals$`, "m"),
    );
  }
  assert.match(run.stdout, /^contrast-audit: \d+ stylesheets, 0 failing claims, 0 colour literals outside token blocks$/m);
});

test("app/styles/tokens.css is the only token file under app/; every other stylesheet is a consumer", () => {
  const sheets = appSheets();
  assert.deepEqual(
    sheets.filter((sheet) => sheet.kind === "tokens").map((sheet) => sheet.path),
    [TOKEN_FILE],
    "a stylesheet whose first rule is `:root {` would be read for claims and masked for literals",
  );
  const tokens = sheets.find((sheet) => sheet.path === TOKEN_FILE);
  const blocks = tokenBlocks(tokens.css);
  assert.ok(blocks.light && blocks.dark, "tokens.css has a :root block and one prefers-color-scheme: dark remap");
  assert.equal(blocks.forced, null, "forced-colors blocks live in the consumer that owns the mark, never in tokens.css");
  assert.ok(
    auditStylesheet(tokens.css, tokens).claims.length >= 75,
    "every ink, state pair, mark and focus ring documents its ratio in both blocks",
  );
  const globals = sheets.find((sheet) => sheet.path === "app/globals.css");
  assert.ok(globals, "app/globals.css is walked");
  assert.equal(globals.kind, "consumer", "globals.css opens with @import + resets, never :root");
  const byPath = new Map(collectStylesheets(root).map((sheet) => [sheet.path, sheet]));
  for (const page of PAGES) {
    const sheet = byPath.get(`deploy/railway/pages/${page}.html`);
    assert.ok(sheet, `${page}.html is walked`);
    assert.equal(sheet.kind, "tokens", `${page}.html inlines its own :root`);
    const pageBlocks = tokenBlocks(sheet.css);
    assert.ok(pageBlocks.light, `${page}.html has a :root block`);
    assert.equal(pageBlocks.dark, null, `${page}.html has no dark block — an absent block is null, not the first block`);
    assert.equal(pageBlocks.forced, null, `${page}.html has no forced-colors block`);
  }
});

test("no new stylesheet references a legacy alias", () => {
  const names = legacyAliasNames();
  assert.ok(names.length >= 100, `the alias block maps every pre-Wave-3 name (${names.length})`);
  assert.ok(names.includes("--white") && names.includes("--font-ui"), "the banner is followed by the alias declarations");
  const scanned = [];
  for (const sheet of appSheets()) {
    if (sheet.path === TOKEN_FILE || LEGACY_STYLESHEETS.has(sheet.path)) continue;
    scanned.push(sheet.path);
    for (const name of names) {
      assert.doesNotMatch(
        sheet.css,
        new RegExp(`var\\(${escapeRegExp(name)}[\\s,)]`),
        `${sheet.path} references the legacy alias ${name}`,
      );
    }
  }
  // Vacuous until the first new stylesheet exists (Task 4 adds fonts.css);
  // from then on every new file under app/ is scanned.
  assert.deepEqual(
    scanned,
    appSheets().map((sheet) => sheet.path).filter((p) => p !== TOKEN_FILE && !LEGACY_STYLESHEETS.has(p)),
  );
});

test("a consumer stylesheet masks nothing: a literal anywhere in it fails, even inside a :root", () => {
  const report = auditStylesheet(".card { color: #123456; }\n:root { --x: #ffffff; }\n", {
    path: "app/styles/example.css",
    kind: "consumer",
  });
  assert.equal(report.claims.length, 0);
  assert.deepEqual(report.literals.map((l) => `${l.line}:${l.text}`), ["1:#123456", "2:#ffffff"]);
});

test("a colour literal injected into a page fails the run and is named by file and line", () => {
  const source = readFileSync(path.join(root, "deploy", "railway", "pages", "login.html"), "utf8");
  const injected = source.replace(".btn-primary:hover {", ".btn-primary:hover { color: #123456;");
  assert.notEqual(injected, source, "the hover rule is where the literal is injected");
  const line = injected.split("\n").findIndex((text) => text.includes("#123456")) + 1;
  const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "contrast-audit-"));
  try {
    const copy = path.join(dir, "login.html");
    writeFileSync(copy, injected);
    const run = runAudit(copy);
    assert.equal(run.status, 1, run.stdout + run.stderr);
    assert.match(
      run.stdout,
      new RegExp(`^  FAIL .*login\\.html:L${line} colour literal outside token blocks: #123456$`, "m"),
    );
    assert.match(run.stdout, /^contrast-audit: 1 stylesheets, 0 failing claims, 1 colour literals outside token blocks$/m);
  } finally {
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create `app/styles/tokens.css`**

Write the file below exactly (lowercase hex; every ratio in a comment is the audit tool's own measurement — a ratio you change is a ratio the tool will reject). The file must begin, after the header comment, with the literal text `:root {` (one space) — `isTokenStylesheet` classifies it as the token file on that alone. The LEGACY ALIASES `:root` sits AFTER the dark block so `tokenBlocks` never reads it, and it holds only `var()` / `rgb(var())` values and keywords (`transparent`, `linear`, `0ms`, `0px`, `1`), so `literalsIn` finds nothing in it and no claim can ever be written against it (a claim on a `var()` token is "unresolved" and fails the run).

```css
/*
 * iTrack design tokens — the professional's ledger (spec §5.1, mockup A).
 * This is the ONE token file tools/contrast-audit.mjs reads claims from: its
 * first rule is `:root {` and the dark remap is `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`.
 * No @font-face, @layer or @import may precede the :root block (fonts live in fonts.css).
 */
:root {
  /*
   * SURFACES — bone paper, a deeper paper for the rail and the phone app bar,
   * and a warm near-white card. Cards separate by a --line hairline and a
   * 12px radius, not by elevation (paper to card is 1.10 by design).
   */
  --paper: #f5f2ea;
  --paper-deep: #ebe7dc;
  --card: #fffdf8;

  /*
   * INK — body and muted. Every ink clears AA on every surface and soft fill
   * it is approved for; the dark block restates each ratio.
   *   --ink        15.5:1 on --paper, 14.1:1 on --paper-deep, 17.1:1 on --card
   *   --ink-muted  6.1:1 on --paper, 5.6:1 on --paper-deep, 6.8:1 on --card,
   *                5.6:1 on --accent-soft, 5.7:1 on --state-overdue-soft,
   *                6.0:1 on --state-due-soon-soft, 5.8:1 on --state-complete-soft
   */
  --ink: #1c1a17;
  --ink-muted: #5e5a52;

  /*
   * LINES — --line is the structural hairline (decorative, no claim). --line-strong
   * is the perceivable boundary a text input wears (a11y-05), at least 3 to 1 on card and paper.
   *   --line-strong  3.9:1 on --card, 3.6:1 on --paper, 3.2:1 on --paper-deep
   */
  --line: #dad5c8;
  --line-strong: #847f74;

  /*
   * ACCENT — one fountain-pen blue. Text on every paper surface, a filled
   * control carrying --on-accent, and the "on track" state. --on-accent is also
   * the label on a destructive (--state-overdue) fill.
   *   --accent        7.3:1 on --paper, 6.6:1 on --paper-deep, 8.0:1 on --card, 6.7:1 on --accent-soft
   *                   6.6:1 on --track (mark)
   *   --accent-hover  10.4:1 on --paper, 11.5:1 on --card
   *   --on-accent     8.0:1 on --accent, 11.5:1 on --accent-hover, 6.4:1 on --state-overdue
   */
  --accent: #2743b8;
  --accent-hover: #1b2f86;
  --accent-soft: #e3e8fa;
  --on-accent: #fffdf8;

  /*
   * SEMANTIC STATE — separate from the accent. Each state is a solid ink
   * (pill text, ring arc, bar fill, timeline dot stroke) with a soft fill
   * (pill and dot fill). Neutral is --ink-muted on a --paper-deep fill.
   *   --state-overdue    5.4:1 on --state-overdue-soft, 6.4:1 on --card, 5.8:1 on --paper
   *                      5.3:1 on --track (mark)
   *   --state-due-soon   5.2:1 on --state-due-soon-soft, 5.8:1 on --card, 5.3:1 on --paper
   *                      4.8:1 on --track (mark)
   *   --state-complete   5.5:1 on --state-complete-soft, 6.5:1 on --card, 5.9:1 on --paper
   *                      5.3:1 on --track (mark)
   *   --state-neutral    5.6:1 on --state-neutral-soft, 6.8:1 on --card
   *                      5.6:1 on --track (mark)
   */
  --state-overdue: #b3261e;
  --state-overdue-soft: #fbe4e2;
  --state-due-soon: #8a5a00;
  --state-due-soon-soft: #fbefd3;
  --state-complete: #22694e;
  --state-complete-soft: #ddf0e6;
  --state-neutral: #5e5a52;
  --state-neutral-soft: #ebe7dc;
  /* The due-soon row edge from the mockup: decorative only, never the sole signal. */
  --edge-due-soon: #e5c98a;

  /*
   * INSTRUMENTS — the unfilled trough of a ring or bar (a trough, never a
   * border), and the 1px minimum marker drawn across a credit bar.
   */
  --track: #ebe7dc;
  --marker: #5e5a52;

  /*
   * INVERSE SURFACE — the "Best next action" card and the toast are the other
   * scheme's page: ink in light, paper in dark. Text on it flips with it.
   *   --on-inverse         15.5:1 on --inverse-surface
   *   --on-inverse-muted   9.8:1 on --inverse-surface
   *   --accent-on-inverse  7.6:1 on --inverse-surface
   */
  --inverse-surface: #1c1a17;
  --on-inverse: #f5f2ea;
  --on-inverse-muted: #c9c2b4;
  --accent-on-inverse: #93a6ff;

  /*
   * FOCUS — one ring, the accent, 3px solid with a 2px offset, on every
   * focusable thing including form fields (a11y-06).
   *   --focus-ring  7.3:1 on --paper (mark), 8.0:1 on --card (mark)
   */
  --focus-ring: #2743b8;

  /*
   * CHANNEL TRIPLES — for the few surfaces painted at an alpha (the modal
   * scrim, a lift over a panel, a shadow). Used only as rgb(var(--x) / a).
   */
  --paper-rgb: 245 242 234;
  --card-rgb: 255 253 248;
  --ink-rgb: 28 26 23;
  --accent-rgb: 39 67 184;
  --line-rgb: 218 213 200;
  --on-inverse-rgb: 245 242 234;
  --lift-rgb: 255 253 248;
  --shade-rgb: 28 26 23;
  --scrim: rgba(28, 26, 23, 0.55);

  /* SHADOWS — ink at low alpha; used sparingly (modal, toast, dragged card). */
  --shadow-sm: 0 1px 2px rgba(28, 26, 23, 0.06);
  --shadow-md: 0 8px 24px rgba(28, 26, 23, 0.1);
  --shadow-lg: 0 24px 64px rgba(28, 26, 23, 0.16);

  /* RADII — 8 controls, 12 cards, 16 sheets and modals, pill. */
  --radius-sm: 8px;
  --radius-md: 12px;
  --radius-lg: 16px;
  --radius-pill: 999px;

  /*
   * TYPE — three faces, self-hosted (fonts.css, Task 4). Display for titles,
   * hero numerals and ring labels; body for everything else; mono for dates,
   * ids and any column of digits. The Fallback faces are metric-matched
   * local() fonts declared in fonts.css so the swap does not reflow.
   */
  --font-display: "Bricolage Grotesque", "Bricolage Grotesque Fallback", "Atkinson Hyperlegible", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;
  --font-body: "Atkinson Hyperlegible", "Atkinson Hyperlegible Fallback", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;
  --font-mono: "iTrack Mono", "iTrack Mono Fallback", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace;
  --tracking-display: -0.02em;
  --tracking-eyebrow: 0.08em;

  /*
   * TYPE SCALE — rem (a11y-14), nine steps, spec §5.1. Body is --text-md
   * (1rem). Nothing declares a font-size below --text-2xs. --text-control is
   * the single px in the system: the iOS zoom floor for editable values.
   */
  --text-2xs: 0.75rem;
  --text-xs: 0.8125rem;
  --text-sm: 0.875rem;
  --text-md: 1rem;
  --text-lg: 1.125rem;
  --text-xl: 1.375rem;
  --text-2xl: 1.75rem;
  --text-3xl: 2.25rem;
  --text-4xl: 3rem;
  --text-control: 16px;

  /* CONTROLS AND TAP TARGETS */
  --control-height: 40px;
  --control-height-lg: 44px;
  --control-height-sm: 32px;
  --tap-min: 44px;
  --tap-comfortable: 48px;

  /*
   * SHELL — the desktop rail, the content column (its content box: the
   * padding sits outside --content-max), the Home ledger's right column
   * (mockup README "Desktop shell": minmax(0, 1fr) 380px, 28px gap — declared
   * here, consumed in Wave 4 with the Home extraction), the phone bar.
   */
  --rail-width: 232px;
  --content-max: 1120px;
  --ledger-aside-width: 380px;
  --bottom-nav-height: 76px;

  /*
   * MOTION — three moments (spec §5.1); everything else is instant.
   * --duration-fill: a credit bar filling, and a ring arc completing.
   * --duration-complete: the check drawing after the arc completes.
   * --duration-fold: a card folding to the ledger row (Wave 4).
   * The reduced-motion block zeroes the durations.
   */
  --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);
  --duration-fill: 400ms;
  --duration-complete: 320ms;
  --duration-fold: 360ms;
}

/*
 * DARK SCHEME — the same ledger after dark. Paper darkens, ink lightens, the
 * accent moves to the bright end of the same blue, and the inverse card
 * becomes bone paper. Every token above is restated where it changes.
 */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --paper: #15130f;
    --paper-deep: #0f0e0b;
    --card: #1f1c16;

    /*
     *   --ink        15.2:1 on --paper, 15.8:1 on --paper-deep, 13.9:1 on --card
     *   --ink-muted  7.25:1 on --paper, 7.5:1 on --paper-deep, 6.6:1 on --card,
     *                5.6:1 on --accent-soft, 5.8:1 on --state-overdue-soft,
     *                5.4:1 on --state-due-soon-soft, 5.3:1 on --state-complete-soft
     */
    --ink: #ede8dc;
    --ink-muted: #a8a196;

    /*
     *   --line-strong  3.5:1 on --card, 3.9:1 on --paper
     */
    --line: #332f27;
    --line-strong: #78725f;

    /*
     *   --accent        8.1:1 on --paper, 8.4:1 on --paper-deep, 7.4:1 on --card, 6.3:1 on --accent-soft
     *                   5.8:1 on --track (mark)
     *   --accent-hover  10.6:1 on --paper, 9.7:1 on --card
     *   --on-accent     8.1:1 on --accent, 10.6:1 on --accent-hover, 7.6:1 on --state-overdue
     */
    --accent: #93a6ff;
    --accent-hover: #b4c1ff;
    --accent-soft: #1e2750;
    --on-accent: #15130f;

    /*
     *   --state-overdue    6.1:1 on --state-overdue-soft, 7.0:1 on --card, 7.6:1 on --paper
     *                      5.5:1 on --track (mark)
     *   --state-due-soon   7.5:1 on --state-due-soon-soft, 9.2:1 on --card, 10.05:1 on --paper
     *                      7.2:1 on --track (mark)
     *   --state-complete   7.2:1 on --state-complete-soft, 8.9:1 on --card, 9.7:1 on --paper
     *                      7.0:1 on --track (mark)
     *   --state-neutral    5.2:1 on --state-neutral-soft, 6.6:1 on --card
     *                      5.2:1 on --track (mark)
     */
    --state-overdue: #f08a80;
    --state-overdue-soft: #3d1f1c;
    --state-due-soon: #e6b85c;
    --state-due-soon-soft: #3a2a12;
    --state-complete: #7fcba4;
    --state-complete-soft: #163326;
    --state-neutral: #a8a196;
    --state-neutral-soft: #332f27;
    --edge-due-soon: #6b5320;

    --track: #332f27;
    --marker: #a8a196;

    /*
     *   --on-inverse         14.2:1 on --inverse-surface
     *   --on-inverse-muted   5.6:1 on --inverse-surface
     *   --accent-on-inverse  6.7:1 on --inverse-surface
     */
    --inverse-surface: #ede8dc;
    --on-inverse: #1c1a17;
    --on-inverse-muted: #5e5a52;
    --accent-on-inverse: #2743b8;

    /*
     *   --focus-ring  8.1:1 on --paper (mark), 7.4:1 on --card (mark)
     */
    --focus-ring: #93a6ff;

    --paper-rgb: 21 19 15;
    --card-rgb: 31 28 22;
    --ink-rgb: 237 232 220;
    --accent-rgb: 147 166 255;
    --line-rgb: 51 47 39;
    --on-inverse-rgb: 28 26 23;
    --lift-rgb: 237 232 220;
    --shade-rgb: 0 0 0;
    --scrim: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.66);

    --shadow-sm: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45);
    --shadow-md: 0 8px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
    --shadow-lg: 0 24px 64px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.62);
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  :root {
    --duration-fill: 0ms;
    --duration-complete: 0ms;
    --duration-fold: 0ms;
  }
}

/*
 * LEGACY ALIASES — BANNED FOR NEW CODE. Every pre-Wave-3 token name, mapped
 * onto the new palette so app/ITrackApp.tsx keeps rendering until Wave 4
 * extracts each screen. Wave 4 deletes this block; a new stylesheet may not
 * reference any name in it (tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs). Values are var()
 * references only — no literals, no claims.
 */
:root {
  --white: var(--card);
  --ink-deep: var(--ink);
  --ink-soft: var(--accent);
  --ink-label: var(--ink);
  --ink-faint: var(--ink-muted);
  --ink-placeholder: var(--ink-muted);
  --ink-quiet: var(--ink-muted);
  --ink-warm: var(--ink-muted);
  --ink-amber: var(--state-due-soon);
  --ink-amber-quiet: var(--state-due-soon);
  --ink-amber-deep: var(--state-due-soon);
  --ink-coral: var(--state-overdue);
  --ink-coral-deep: var(--state-overdue);
  --ink-coral-quiet: var(--state-overdue);
  --ink-coral-faint: var(--state-overdue);
  --ink-tint: var(--accent);
  --ink-tint-link: var(--accent);
  --ink-tint-quiet: var(--accent);
  --ink-tint-deep: var(--accent);
  --ink-blue: var(--accent);
  --accent-ink: var(--accent);
  --accent-bright: var(--accent-on-inverse);
  --accent-control: var(--accent);
  --accent-control-hover: var(--accent-hover);
  --tint: var(--accent-soft);
  --tint-bright: var(--accent-soft);
  --amber: var(--state-due-soon);
  --amber-soft: var(--state-due-soon-soft);
  --coral: var(--state-overdue);
  --coral-soft: var(--state-overdue-soft);
  --danger: var(--state-overdue);
  --danger-hover: var(--state-overdue);
  --ink-surface: var(--inverse-surface);
  --ink-surface-deep: var(--inverse-surface);
  --ink-surface-hover: var(--inverse-surface);
  --ink-surface-press: var(--inverse-surface);
  --ink-surface-inset: var(--inverse-surface);
  --on-dark: var(--on-inverse);
  --on-dark-muted: var(--on-inverse-muted);
  --on-dark-faint: var(--on-inverse-muted);
  --on-mark: var(--card);
  --wash: var(--paper);
  --wash-deep: var(--paper-deep);
  --wash-tint: var(--accent-soft);
  --wash-amber: var(--state-due-soon-soft);
  --wash-amber-soft: var(--state-due-soon-soft);
  --wash-coral: var(--state-overdue-soft);
  --wash-coral-deep: var(--state-overdue-soft);
  --chip: var(--paper-deep);
  --chip-tint: var(--accent-soft);
  --chip-coral: var(--state-overdue-soft);
  --chip-coral-deep: var(--state-overdue-soft);
  --chip-blue: var(--accent-soft);
  --highlight-amber: var(--state-due-soon-soft);
  --amber-card-from: var(--state-due-soon-soft);
  --track-quiet: var(--track);
  --track-tint: var(--track);
  --line-soft: var(--line);
  --edge: var(--line);
  --edge-soft: var(--line);
  --edge-tint: var(--line);
  --edge-quiet: var(--line);
  --edge-mark: var(--line-strong);
```

```ts
export const viewport: Viewport = {
  // This colours the browser and OS chrome — the address bar and the
  // standalone status bar — not anything the app paints. Both schemes now
  // name the page itself (--paper), which is what the mobile header under the
  // bar is painted with at `rgb(var(--paper-rgb) / 0.9)`: on a platform where
  // the status bar sits *inside* the app's own canvas, any bar that is not
  // the page reads as a stripe. `light dark` lets the UA render form controls
  // and scrollbars in the matching scheme.
  themeColor: [
    { media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)", color: "#f2f2f7" },
    { media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)", color: "#0b0b0e" },
  ],
  colorScheme: "light dark",
  width: "device-width",
  initialScale: 1,
  viewportFit: "cover",
};
```

Replace them with:

```ts
export const viewport: Viewport = {
  // This colours the browser and OS chrome — the address bar and the
  // standalone status bar — not anything the app paints. Both schemes name
  // --paper-deep, the surface the rail and the phone app bar are painted
  // with (app/styles/tokens.css): on a phone the status bar sits directly on
  // that bar, so a chrome colour that is not the bar's reads as a stripe.
  // `light dark` lets the UA render form controls and scrollbars in the
  // matching scheme.
  themeColor: [
    { media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)", color: "#ebe7dc" },
    { media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)", color: "#0f0e0b" },
  ],
  colorScheme: "light dark",
  width: "device-width",
  initialScale: 1,
  viewportFit: "cover",
};
```

```html
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta
      name="viewport"
      content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"
    />
    <meta
      name="theme-color"
      media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
      content="#ebe7dc"
    />
    <meta
      name="theme-color"
      media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
      content="#0f0e0b"
    />
    <link rel="icon" href="/icon-192.png" />
    <title>iTrack — Offline</title>
    <style>
      /*
        This page is served from the cache with no stylesheet of its own, so it

        no alpha, no haze: the ledger has none. The text clears AA on the card in
        both schemes — 17.1:1 / 13.9:1 for --ink, 6.8:1 / 6.6:1 for --ink-muted —
        as do the button label (15.5:1 / 14.2:1, --on-inverse on --inverse-surface)
        and the mark (7.6:1 / 6.7:1, --accent-on-inverse on --inverse-surface).
        The type stays on the system stack: the woff2 faces are not precached.
      */
      :root {
        color-scheme: light dark;
        font-family: "Atkinson Hyperlegible", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;
        --paper: #f5f2ea;

        display: grid;
        place-items: center;
        padding:

          max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-right))
          calc(24px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))
          max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-left));
        background: var(--paper);
      }
      main {
        width: min(100%, 430px);

      button {

        border-radius: 8px;
        color: var(--on-inverse);
        background: var(--inverse-surface);
        font: inherit;
        font-weight: 700;
      }

      <div class="mark" aria-hidden="true">✦</div>
      <h1>Your renewal record is safe.</h1>
      <p>
```

### Task 2: Split `globals.css` into `app/styles/<screen>.css` + `legacy-shared.css` at pixel parity (snapshot-proven), then the px→rem font-size sweep with its guard (architecture-11, a11y-14)

**Rationale:** spec §5.2 ("per-screen styles in `app/styles/<screen>.css`; `globals.css` shrinks to resets + tokens import") and spec §5.1 ("Type scale in rem"). Finding architecture-11: `app/globals.css` is cross-cut, not dead — every screen's responsive rules live in four trailing media blocks (`@media (max-width: 1040px|820px|540px|340px)`, 139 selectors restated after a base declaration), so a screen can only be extracted once its rules travel with it, and the finding's own recommendation is to do the split as ONE mechanical, parity-proven commit before any restyle. Finding a11y-14: the type scale is px-only (49 `font-size: …px` declarations, one `1.5rem`, no root size), so a browser font-size preference does nothing. The rem sweep is the one restyle that belongs with the move: it touches every file at once and is a Wave 3 gate (Global Constraints, "Type sizes"). Two commits: **A** moves every rule verbatim into its owner and proves 24 snapshots pixel-identical; **B** maps the 49 px sizes onto the nine-step rem scale and lands the guard that keeps them there.

**Line numbers.** Every range in this task is a line range of `app/globals.css` at **main @4bc32b5** — the pre-split file the plan was written against, 6,763 lines.
```ts
import { expect, test } from "./fixtures";

// Pixel-parity proof for a stylesheet reorganisation that is not meant to
// change a single rendered pixel (Task 2's split of globals.css, Task 3's
// Tailwind removal). Off by default: set WAVE3_PARITY=1. Baselines are taken
// on the parent commit with --update-snapshots and live under
// tests/e2e/parity.spec.ts-snapshots/ (gitignored) — they are a local
// instrument, never evidence, and never committed.
//
// Read-only against the demo workspace: it only reads routes and opens the
// Log sheet; nothing is submitted.
test.skip(!process.env.WAVE3_PARITY, "set WAVE3_PARITY=1 to compare against the baseline snapshots");

test("every route renders pixel-identical to the baseline", async ({ page, app }) => {
  // The greeting (dayPart), the countdowns and every date read the clock:
  // pin it so a baseline taken before noon still matches a run after it.
  await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date("2026-09-15T15:00:00"));
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: "reduce" });
  const detailId = (await app.workspace()).credentials[0].id;
  const routes: Array<[string, string]> = [
    ["home", "/"],
    ["credentials", "/credentials"],
    ["credential-detail", `/credentials/${detailId}`],
    ["history", "/history"],
    ["profile", "/profile"],
  ];
  for (const [slug, route] of routes) {
    await app.goto(route);
    await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot(`${slug}.png`, {
      fullPage: true,
      animations: "disabled",
      maxDiffPixels: 0,
    });
  }
  await app.goto("/");
  await app.openLog();
  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot("log-activity.png", {
    animations: "disabled",
    maxDiffPixels: 0,
  });
  app.expectNoErrors();
});
```

Write the generator to the scratchpad. It copies every moved range VERBATIM from the reference copy (asserting fifteen anchor lines first, and that no range starts or ends on a blank line), builds each file as header + banner + `base(...)` runs + `media(query, ...)` re-wraps, and rebuilds `globals.css` from the working file by anchor text so Task 1's reset edits are preserved. Every range is one the plan named above.

```bash
cat > "$SCRATCH/split-globals.py" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Wave 3 Task 2, commit A — split app/globals.css into app/styles/<owner>.css at pixel parity.

Every moved rule is copied VERBATIM from the pre-split reference copy of app/globals.css
(main @4bc32b5: `git show 4bc32b5:app/globals.css`), whose line numbers are the ones the
Wave 3 plan cites. Task 1 touched none of the moved lines (it edited 1-607, 624-633,
709-717, 746-765, 5798-5800 and 6690-6703 — all of them resets that STAY in globals.css or
lines that are deleted), so copying from the reference is exact. The shrunken globals.css
is rebuilt from the WORKING file so Task 1's reset edits are kept, not retyped.

Usage:  python3 split-globals.py <worktree-root> <reference-copy>
"""
import pathlib
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
REF = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text().splitlines()
assert len(REF) == 6763, f"reference copy has {len(REF)} lines, expected 6763 (main @4bc32b5)"
for line_no, text in {1: '@import "tailwindcss";', 609: "* {", 767: ".app-shell {", 1041: ".renewal-hero {",
                      2468: "/*", 3944: ".modal-backdrop {", 5624: "/*", 5697: "@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {",
                      5797: "@media (max-width: 1040px) {", 5838: "@media (max-width: 820px) {",
                      6202: "@media (max-width: 540px) {", 6612: "@media (max-width: 340px) {",
                      6660: "@media (pointer: coarse) {", 6729: "@media (forced-colors: active) {",
                      6743: "/* Error fallback (ErrorBoundary, app/error.tsx, app/not-found.tsx). */"}.items():
    assert REF[line_no - 1] == text, f"reference L{line_no} is {REF[line_no - 1]!r}, expected {text!r}"


def ref(a, b):
    """Lines a..b of the reference copy, inclusive, 1-based, verbatim."""
    assert 1 <= a <= b <= len(REF), (a, b)
    assert REF[a - 1].strip() and REF[b - 1].strip(), f"range {a}-{b} starts or ends on a blank line"
    return "\n".join(REF[a - 1:b])


def base(*ranges):
    """Top-level rules, in the given order, one blank line between runs."""
    return "\n\n".join(ref(a, b) for a, b in ranges)


def media(query, *ranges):
    """Rules that sat inside one of the four trailing @media blocks (they are already indented
    two spaces in the reference), re-wrapped in the owner file's own block of the same query."""
    return f"{query} {{\n" + "\n\n".join(ref(a, b) for a, b in ranges) + "\n}"


MOVED = ("Moved verbatim from app/globals.css (main @4bc32b5) in Wave 3 Task 2 "
         "(architecture-11); these rules are restyled or extracted in Wave 4.")


def header(owner):
    return f"/* {owner}\n * {MOVED} */"


def banner(name):
    return f"/* ===== {name} ===== */"


HOVER = "@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)"
W1040, W820, W540, W340 = ("@media (max-width: 1040px)", "@media (max-width: 820px)",
                           "@media (max-width: 540px)", "@media (max-width: 340px)")

FILES = {

             (1689, 1707), (1915, 1958), (2269, 2290), (2948, 2976), (3232, 3374), (3804, 3825),
             (5740, 5766), (5768, 5795)),
```

Replace the whole of `tests/helpers/clientSources.mjs` with:

```js
// Walks the client source under app/ for the static source guards: every
// .ts/.tsx/.mts file (readClientSources) and every .css file (readStylesheets).
// It lives under tests/helpers/ (not in a *.test.mjs) so that importing it
// never re-registers another file's tests under `node --test`.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const appDir = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "..", "app");

function walk(dir, out = []) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const full = path.join(dir, entry);
    if (statSync(full).isDirectory()) walk(full, out);
    else if (/\.(tsx?|mts)$/.test(entry)) out.push(full);
  }
  return out;
}

function walkAll(dir, out = []) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const full = path.join(dir, entry);
    if (statSync(full).isDirectory()) walkAll(full, out);
    else out.push(full);
  }
  return out;
}

// `file` is relative to app/ (e.g. "api/workspace/route.ts").
export function readClientSources() {
  return walk(appDir).map((file) => ({ file: path.relative(appDir, file), source: readFileSync(file, "utf8") }));
}

// Every .css under app/ (`file` relative to app/, e.g. "globals.css" or "styles/home.css").
export function readStylesheets() {
  return walkAll(appDir)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith(".css"))
    .map((file) => ({ file: path.relative(appDir, file), source: readFileSync(file, "utf8") }));
}
```

```js
// and consumed only through max(var(--text-control), 1em). Comments are

test("no font-size in px under app/**/*.css except the documented --text-control floor (a11y-14)", () => {
  const blank = (text) => text.replace(/[^\n]/g, " ");
  let scanned = 0;
  let controls = 0;
  for (const { file, source } of readStylesheets()) {
    scanned += 1;
    const code = source.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, blank);
    for (const match of code.matchAll(/^\s*font-size\s*:\s*([^;{}]+);/gm)) {
      assert.doesNotMatch(
        match[1],
        /\b\d*\.?\d+px\b/,
        `${file}: \`${match[0].trim()}\` — use a --text-* token or rem`,
      );
    }
    for (const match of code.matchAll(/^\s*(--text-[a-z0-9-]+)\s*:\s*([^;]+);/gm)) {
      if (match[1] === "--text-control") {
        controls += 1;
        assert.equal(file, "styles/tokens.css", "--text-control is declared in tokens.css only");
        assert.equal(match[2].trim(), "16px", "--text-control is the 16px iOS zoom floor");
        continue;
      }
      assert.match(match[2], /^\s*\d*\.?\d+rem\s*$/, `${file}: ${match[1]} must be declared in rem`);
    }
  }
  assert.ok(scanned >= 9, "walked app/globals.css and app/styles/*.css");
  assert.equal(controls, 1, "--text-control is declared exactly once");
});
```

**Gotchas for this task.**
- CSS `@import` must precede every rule, so all nine imports sit at the top of `globals.css`; Vite inlines them into one built stylesheet in import order — `legacy-shared.css` first, the six screens next, `globals.css`'s own resets last (they are element selectors and `*`, so the cascade change is harmless: the check in the Rationale found no equal-specificity pair between a reset and a moved rule).
- A screen file that re-wraps `@media` rules keeps the original NESTING (one level deep; the reference lines are already indented two spaces). The three at-rules that were nested inside a base run — `@media (hover: hover)` at 1975, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` at 2587, `@supports selector(:has(*))` at 3659 — travel inside their runs untouched.
- The phone Playwright projects (iPhone 13 descriptor, `hasTouch`) match `(pointer: coarse)`, which is why the tap-floor block's position relative to `.draft-safety-note button` / `.mode-switch button` / `.field select` matters for parity and why it ends `log-activity.css`.
- `tools/contrast-audit.mjs` classifies every new file as a consumer (its first rule is a selector), so a single hex or named colour anywhere in them fails the run — the moved rules contain none (the audit passed on the whole file before the split), and the forced-colours keywords are legal only inside `legacy-shared.css`'s own first `@media (forced-colors: active)` block.
- The `norm` check strips comment lines beginning with `*` and `/*`, so the banner and header comments never count; the snapshots are the proof for the `*`-prefixed universal rules it cannot see.
- Never edit, `git add` or commit anything under `tests/e2e/parity.spec.ts-snapshots/`; never run the parity spec with `--update-snapshots` on the changed tree (that would bless the change); after commit B the baselines are stale by design.
- `sed -i ''` (BSD) — GNU's `sed -i` without the empty argument fails on macOS; the `norm` function must `cat` its files because BSD `grep` prefixes file names when given several.

### Task 3: Remove Tailwind (no utility is used): port its preflight into `globals.css` as the explicit reset, delete the PostCSS config and the two devDependencies, snapshot-proven parity (architecture-12)

**Rationale:** spec §5.2 (`globals.css shrinks to resets + tokens import`) and audit finding architecture-12 (Tailwind is imported and compiled on every build but no utility class is used anywhere). Everything below was verified against main @4bc32b5, and the port is designed from what the compiler actually shipped, not from what the source file says:

- **What is there.** `app/globals.css:1` is `@import "tailwindcss";`. `postcss.config.mjs` (7 lines) registers only `@tailwindcss/postcss`. `package.json:34` is `"@tailwindcss/postcss": "4.2.1"`, `:44` is `"tailwindcss": "4.2.1"`; `:50-53` overrides `postcss` 8.5.18 and `sharp` — the `postcss` override stays because Vite 8.0.13 itself depends on `postcss ^8.5.14`. No `@apply`, `@theme`, `@utility` or `@layer` appears in app CSS, there is no `tailwind.config.*`, and all 544 `className` attributes in `app/**/*.tsx` are app classes.
- **What the build ships today** (`dist/client/assets/index-CTlXjY5V.css`, 99,823 bytes, of which the first 7,538 are Tailwind): `@layer theme` declares sixteen custom properties on `:root, :host` — `--font-sans --font-mono --spacing --text-xs --text-sm --text-lg --radius-sm --radius-md --radius-lg --shadow-sm --shadow-md --shadow-lg --default-transition-duration --default-transition-timing-function --default-font-family --default-mono-font-family` — nine of which share a name with the app's own tokens and lose to them only because the theme layer sits below unlayered rules; `@layer base` is the preflight; `@layer utilities` holds 31 utilities that Tailwind's automatic content detection generated from words it found anywhere in the tree (`absolute block border collapse container contents end fixed flex flex-wrap grid grow hidden inline invisible isolate outline relative resize ring shrink sr-only start static sticky table tabular-nums transform transition underline visible`); `@layer properties` plus 26 `@property` rules register the 31 `--tw-*` properties the audit counted. Intersecting those 31 utility names with every string token in the 41 files under `app/**/*.ts(x)` finds exactly two class names: `sr-only` (seven `<span className="sr-only">` sites; the app's own unlayered `.sr-only` at `app/globals.css:719-729` declares every property Tailwind's version does except `clip-path: inset(50%)`, and a 1×1 px absolutely positioned overflow-hidden box clipped to `rect(0, 0, 0, 0)` paints nothing either way) and `transition` (`ruleReviewClass`, `app/ITrackApp.tsx:603-612`, returns it for `transition_rule_check_assigned_cycle`; applied on `.verified-chip` at `:5415` and `:8756`, where Tailwind's `.transition` added a 150 ms colour/shadow transition — identical at rest, and mockup decision 6 wants no such motion). Every other hit (`fixed`, `start`, `end`, `visible`, `hidden`, `contents`) is copy or JavaScript, not a class. So dropping the theme, utilities and properties layers changes no rendered pixel.
- **What would break without the port.** The preflight zeroes `margin`/`padding` and sets `border: 0 solid` on `*`, makes `h1–h6` inherit size and weight, unstyles `ol, ul, menu`, makes `img, svg, video, canvas…` `display: block`, gives form controls `background-color: transparent` and `border-radius: 0`, and hides `[hidden]` with `!important` — and the 6,700 legacy lines were written on top of every one of those (the `.icon` svgs inside inline-flex buttons rely on `display: block`, `.button` on the zeroed border). The removal therefore ships the preflight itself as the explicit reset in the same commit, and Task 2's parity spec proves nothing moved.
- **The preflight and its `--theme()` reads.** `node_modules/tailwindcss/preflight.css` is 393 lines, sha256 `fa2d5ae43ae561061b7ce348b89636dbdc6cd71ab5992d4e1cdd046d0b4f28f9`, MIT (Tailwind Labs, Inc.). `--theme(` appears at lines 33-42 (`html, :host` font-family), 43, 44, 113-123 (`code, kbd, samp, pre` font-family), 124, 125. The shipped CSS resolves them to `font-family: var(--default-font-family, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, …)`, `font-feature-settings: var(--default-font-feature-settings, normal)`, `font-variation-settings: var(--default-font-variation-settings, normal)` and the mono equivalents; `theme.css:494-499` points `--default-font-feature-settings`/`--default-font-variation-settings` at `--font-sans--font-feature-settings`/`…-variation-settings`, which nothing defines, so both compute to `normal`. `body` sets `font-family: var(--font-body)` (Task 1) and every form control inherits, so the `html` face is never visible: `var(--font-body)` there is a no-op for parity and the right value on its own terms. No `<code>`, `<pre>`, `<kbd>` or `<samp>` is rendered by any file under `app/` today, so `var(--font-mono)` on that rule changes nothing until Task 12's "Technical details" `<pre>`, which should be mono.
- **One more substitution, for Task 2's guard.** Task 2's font-size guard (global constraints: every `font-size` under `app/**/*.css` is a `var(--text-*)` token or a `rem`/`%`/`em` value; the single px is `--text-control: 16px`) would read the preflight's `h1–h6 { font-size: inherit }`. It is ported as `font-size: 1em` — for `font-size`, `1em` of the parent's computed size is exactly what `inherit` computes to — so the guard reads it like every other size. The other three `font-size` declarations in the preflight (`1em` on code, `80%` on small, `75%` on sub/sup) already comply.
- **Layering.** The block stays inside `@layer base`, exactly as `tailwindcss/index.css:534` ships it: unlayered app rules beat layered ones at any specificity, which is what preserves parity — unlayered, the preflight's `border: 0 solid` and `h1 { font-size: 1em }` would win over legacy rules of equal specificity that used to beat the layered preflight. The preflight's one `!important` (`[hidden]`) keeps winning over unlayered `!important` declarations exactly as today (important declarations invert layer order). A single layer needs no `@layer theme, base, components, utilities;` order statement.
- **The toolchain after removal.** Vite's `css.transformer` defaults to `"postcss"` (`node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:20374`) and inlines CSS `@import`s itself whether or not a `postcss.config.*` exists; the client bundle is minified by Lightning CSS (`build.cssMinify`, `:32960`) — the split `::file-selector-button` rules and the `color: currentColor` placeholder fallback visible in the shipped base layer are that kind of targets-based rewriting, applied by the build, never in source; the dev server (what the parity spec sees) serves the source as written. A dry run of `npm uninstall --package-lock-only tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss` on copies of the two manifests (npm 11.11.0 under Node 22.22.0, no network needed) removes exactly these lockfile entries: `tailwindcss`, `@tailwindcss/postcss`, `@tailwindcss/node`, the thirteen `@tailwindcss/oxide*` packages and their six nested wasm helpers, `@alloc/quick-lru`, `jiti`, and the hoisted `lightningcss` 1.31.1 with its eleven platform packages — those belonged to `@tailwindcss/node`; Vite keeps its own nested `node_modules/vite/node_modules/lightningcss` (^1.32.0, `package-lock.json:10144`) — about 630 lines, deletions only, `postcss` untouched. `README.md` mentions neither Tailwind nor PostCSS, so it does not change.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing test — `tests/no-tailwind.test.mjs`**

The parity spec passes before and after by design (that is its point); the test that fails first is the gate that keeps Tailwind out. It reads `package.json`, the presence of `postcss.config.mjs` and the built stylesheet — project configuration and build output, never client source, so `tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs`'s no-source-read guard is untouched. `npm test`'s `tests/*.test.mjs` glob picks the file up.

```js
// architecture-12: Tailwind was imported and compiled on every build while no
// utility class was ever used, so Wave 3 removed it and ported its preflight
// into app/globals.css as the explicit reset (Task 3). At main @4bc32b5 the
// client stylesheet opened with Tailwind's theme/base/utilities/properties
// layers and 31 `--tw-*` properties — 7.5 kB before the first app token. This
// gate keeps the toolchain and the runtime gone. package.json and
// postcss.config.mjs are project configuration, not client source, and the
// second test reads build output, so nothing here trips the source-read guard.
// `npm test` builds before running this file; with no dist at all the dist
// half is vacuously true, like tests/dist-hygiene.test.mjs.
import test from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const root = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");

test("no Tailwind package is declared and no PostCSS config remains (architecture-12)", () => {
  const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(root, "package.json"), "utf8"));
  const declared = [
    ...Object.keys(pkg.dependencies ?? {}),
    ...Object.keys(pkg.devDependencies ?? {}),
  ];
  assert.deepEqual(
    declared.filter((name) => /tailwind/i.test(name)),
    [],
    "package.json still declares a Tailwind package — `npm uninstall tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss` under the Node 22 PATH",
  );
  assert.ok(
    !existsSync(path.join(root, "postcss.config.mjs")),
    "postcss.config.mjs only ever registered @tailwindcss/postcss — delete it; Vite needs no PostCSS config for plain CSS and inlines the @imports itself",
  );
});

test("the built client stylesheet carries no Tailwind runtime (architecture-12)", () => {
  const assets = path.join(root, "dist", "client", "assets");
  if (!existsSync(assets)) return;
  const sheets = readdirSync(assets).filter((name) => name.endsWith(".css"));
  assert.ok(sheets.length > 0, "the client build emits at least one stylesheet under dist/client/assets");
  for (const name of sheets) {
    const css = readFileSync(path.join(assets, name), "utf8");
    assert.doesNotMatch(css, /--tw-/, `${name}: Tailwind's --tw-* properties are back`);
    assert.doesNotMatch(
      css,
      /@layer\s+(theme|components|utilities|properties)\b/,
      `${name}: a Tailwind cascade layer is back — the only layer the app declares is \`@layer base\` (app/globals.css)`,
    );
  }
});
```
