- [ ] **Step 3: `app/styles/instruments.css` — one state map, four instruments, two motion moments, its own forced-colours block — imported after `primitives.css`, and the audit proves it clean**

Create `app/styles/instruments.css` (a consumer for `tools/contrast-audit.mjs`: its first rule is `.instrument`, not `:root {`; no hex, no `rgb()` without `var(--`, no named colour; system colour keywords only inside its own `@media (forced-colors: active)` block; no legacy alias name — `tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs`'s alias guard fails on one; every `font-size` is a `--text-*` token):

```css
/*
 * Instruments (spec §5.1): CycleRing, CreditBar, StatusPill, DeadlineTimeline.
 * One state map, three motion moments (two here, the card fold is Wave 4).
 * A consumer stylesheet: first-class tokens only — no literal, no legacy alias.
 */

/* STATE MAP — every instrument reads --state-ink / --state-soft from here */
.instrument {
  --state-ink: var(--state-neutral);
  --state-soft: var(--state-neutral-soft);
}

.instrument[data-state="overdue"] {
  --state-ink: var(--state-overdue);
  --state-soft: var(--state-overdue-soft);
}

.instrument[data-state="due-soon"] {
  --state-ink: var(--state-due-soon);
  --state-soft: var(--state-due-soon-soft);
}

.instrument[data-state="on-track"] {
  --state-ink: var(--accent);
  --state-soft: var(--accent-soft);
}

.instrument[data-state="submitted"],
.instrument[data-state="complete"] {
  --state-ink: var(--state-complete);
  --state-soft: var(--state-complete-soft);
}

/*
 * CYCLE RING — mockup: 72 / 56 / 40 px, stroke 7 / 6 / 5, the track is the
 * paper-deep trough (--track), the arc the state ink, the numeral in the
 * display face. Sized in rem so it follows the root font size; the geometry
 * lives in the SVG viewBox (app/lib/instruments.ts RING_SIZES).
 */
.cycle-ring {
  display: inline-grid;
  flex: none;
  place-items: center;
}

.cycle-ring[data-size="72"] {
  width: 4.5rem;
  height: 4.5rem;
}

.cycle-ring[data-size="56"] {
  width: 3.5rem;
  height: 3.5rem;
}

.cycle-ring[data-size="40"] {
  width: 2.5rem;
  height: 2.5rem;
}

.cycle-ring svg {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
}

.cycle-ring-track {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--track);
}

/* Complete: the trough takes the state's soft colour under a full arc (desktop artboard). */
.cycle-ring[data-state="complete"] .cycle-ring-track {
  stroke: var(--state-soft);
}

.cycle-ring-arc {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--state-ink);
  stroke-linecap: round;
}

.cycle-ring-label {
  fill: var(--ink);
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-weight: 700;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  letter-spacing: var(--tracking-display);
}

.cycle-ring-check {
  fill: none;
  stroke: var(--state-ink);
  stroke-linecap: round;
  stroke-linejoin: round;
}

/* CREDIT BAR — mockup: a 6px trough, the fill in the state ink, a 1px minimum marker */
.credit-bar {
  position: relative;
  height: 6px;
  border-radius: 3px;
  background: var(--track);
}

.credit-bar[data-state="complete"] {
  background: var(--state-soft);
}

.credit-bar-fill {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0 auto 0 0;
  border-radius: inherit;
  background: var(--state-ink);
}

.credit-bar[data-overflow="true"] .credit-bar-fill {
  background: var(--state-overdue);
}

.credit-bar-mark {
  position: absolute;
  top: -3px;
  width: 1px;
  height: 12px;
  background: var(--marker);
}

/*
 * STATUS PILL — mockup .pill: soft fill + state ink, 3px 9px, pill radius,
 * 0.75rem bold (the artboard's 11px rounds up to the scale floor). The
 * compact form is an 8px dot with its text visually hidden — a styleguide
 * sample only this wave: every mounted pill, the check-in rows included,
 * shows its state word, so the state is never colour alone for anyone
 * (a11y-11; WCAG 1.4.1 — a dot's fill is colour alone for a sighted reader).
 */
.status-pill {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 6px;
  border-radius: var(--radius-pill);
  background: var(--state-soft);
  color: var(--state-ink);
  font-family: var(--font-body);
  font-size: var(--text-2xs);
  font-weight: 700;
  line-height: 1.25;
  padding: 3px 9px;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.status-pill[data-compact="true"] {
  width: 8px;
  height: 8px;
  padding: 0;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--state-ink);
}

/*
 * DEADLINE TIMELINE — mockup: a 340×92 plot, a 2px axis with quarter ticks,
 * a dashed "today" line, one circle per deadline (r 8 due soon / overdue,
 * r 6 otherwise) with its name and mono date above. The circles are 44px
 * buttons in an HTML list laid over the decorative SVG.
 */
.deadline-timeline {
  margin: 0;
}

.deadline-timeline-plot {
  position: relative;
}

.deadline-timeline-plot svg {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
}

.deadline-timeline-axis,
.deadline-timeline-tick {
  stroke: var(--line);
}

.deadline-timeline-axis {
  stroke-width: 2;
}

.deadline-timeline-tick-label {
  fill: var(--ink-muted);
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--text-2xs);
}

.deadline-timeline-today {
  stroke: var(--ink);
  stroke-width: 1.5;
  stroke-dasharray: 3 3;
}

.deadline-timeline-today-label {
  fill: var(--ink);
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--text-2xs);
}

.deadline-timeline-marker-name {
  fill: var(--ink);
  font-family: var(--font-body);
  font-size: var(--text-2xs);
  font-weight: 700;
}

.deadline-timeline-marker-date {
  fill: var(--ink-muted);
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--text-2xs);
}

.deadline-timeline-list {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

/* Each item sits on the axis (y 52 of 92); its `left` is inline, x / 340. */
.deadline-timeline-list > li {
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(52 / 92 * 100%);
  width: 0;
}

/* The 44px hit area, centred on the axis; the visible circle is its ::before. */
.deadline-timeline-hit {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  width: var(--tap-min);
  height: var(--tap-min);
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: transparent;
  cursor: pointer;
  transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
}

.deadline-timeline-hit::before {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  left: 50%;
  width: 16px;
  height: 16px;
  border: 2px solid var(--state-ink);
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--state-soft);
  transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
}

.deadline-timeline-list > li[data-r="6"] .deadline-timeline-hit::before {
  width: 12px;
  height: 12px;
}

.deadline-timeline-tip {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: calc(100% + 4px);
  left: 50%;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--card);
  color: var(--ink);
  font-size: var(--text-2xs);
  padding: 6px 8px;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  visibility: hidden;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.deadline-timeline-hit:hover + .deadline-timeline-tip,
.deadline-timeline-hit:focus-visible + .deadline-timeline-tip {
  visibility: visible;
}

.deadline-timeline figcaption {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 8px;
  margin-top: 8px;
  color: var(--ink-muted);
  font-size: var(--text-xs);
}

.deadline-timeline-range {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}

/*
 * MOTION — the two instrument moments (spec §5.1): a bar filling to its new
 * value, and a ring segment completing followed by the check drawing. The
 * check keyframes carry their own start value: the global reduced-motion
 * freeze clamps every animation to 0.01ms, and `animation: none` must leave
 * the check fully visible.
 */
.credit-bar-fill {
  transition: width var(--duration-fill) var(--ease-out);
}

.cycle-ring[data-state="complete"] .cycle-ring-arc {
  transition: stroke-dasharray var(--duration-fill) var(--ease-out);
}

/* The check draws over --duration-complete (320ms) once the arc's
   --duration-fill has elapsed; no duration literal here — the reduced-motion
   token block zeroes both. */
.cycle-ring[data-motion="complete"] .cycle-ring-check {
  animation: cycle-ring-check-draw var(--duration-complete) var(--ease-out) var(--duration-fill) both;
}

@keyframes cycle-ring-check-draw {
  from {
    stroke-dasharray: 1;
    stroke-dashoffset: 1;
  }

  to {
    stroke-dasharray: 1;
    stroke-dashoffset: 0;
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .credit-bar-fill,
  .cycle-ring-arc,
  .cycle-ring-check {
    transition: none;
    animation: none;
  }
}

.instrument[data-reduced-motion="true"] .credit-bar-fill,
.instrument[data-reduced-motion="true"] .cycle-ring-arc,
.instrument[data-reduced-motion="true"] .cycle-ring-check {
  transition: none;
  animation: none;
}

/* Forced colours: a value carried by a fill alone must survive Windows high contrast. */
@media (forced-colors: active) {
  .cycle-ring-arc,
  .credit-bar-fill {
    forced-color-adjust: none;
    stroke: Highlight;
    background: Highlight;
  }

  .cycle-ring-track,
  .credit-bar {
    forced-color-adjust: none;
    stroke: ButtonFace;
    background: ButtonFace;
  }

  .status-pill[data-compact="true"] {
    background: Highlight;
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The four components**

Create `app/components/instruments/CycleRing.tsx`:

```tsx
"use client";

import { useLayoutEffect, useRef } from "react";
import {
  ringArc,
  type InstrumentState,
  type RingSize,
} from "../../lib/instruments";

export type CycleRingProps = {
  size: RingSize;
  fraction: number;
  percent: number;
  state: InstrumentState;
  label: string;
  valueText?: string;
  showNumeral?: boolean;
  reducedMotion?: boolean;
  className?: string;
};

/*
 * The ring is a progressbar for assistive technology (label + numeric value,
 * as home.spec.ts asserts); the SVG inside is decorative. The geometry —
 * radius, stroke, dash array, numeral size, check path — comes from
 * app/lib/instruments.ts and is never re-derived here.
 */
export function CycleRing({
  size,
  fraction,
  percent,
  state,
  label,
  valueText,
  showNumeral = size !== 40,
  reducedMotion,
  className,
}: CycleRingProps) {
  const arc = ringArc({ size, fraction });
  const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const previous = useRef<number | null>(null);
  // The check draws only when a value crosses complete after mount; a ring
  // that mounts complete renders instantly. Written as a DOM attribute from
  // a layout effect — no state, no ref read during render.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const node = root.current;
    if (
      node &&
      previous.current !== null &&
      previous.current < 1 &&
      arc.fraction >= 1
    ) {
      node.setAttribute("data-motion", "complete");
    }
    previous.current = arc.fraction;
  }, [arc.fraction]);
  return (
    <div
      ref={root}
      className={["instrument", "cycle-ring", className]
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(" ")}
      data-size={size}
      data-state={state}
      data-reduced-motion={reducedMotion ? "true" : undefined}
      role="progressbar"
      aria-label={label}
      aria-valuemin={0}
      aria-valuemax={100}
      aria-valuenow={percent}
      aria-valuetext={valueText}
    >
      <svg viewBox={`0 0 ${size} ${size}`} aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
        <circle
          className="cycle-ring-track"
          cx={arc.centre}
          cy={arc.centre}
          r={arc.r}
          strokeWidth={arc.strokeWidth}
        />
        {arc.fraction > 0 ? (
          <circle
            className="cycle-ring-arc"
            cx={arc.centre}
            cy={arc.centre}
            r={arc.r}
            strokeWidth={arc.strokeWidth}
            strokeDasharray={arc.dashArray}
            transform={`rotate(-90 ${arc.centre} ${arc.centre})`}
          />
        ) : null}
        {state === "complete" ? (
          <path
            className="cycle-ring-check"
            d={arc.check.d}
            strokeWidth={arc.check.strokeWidth}
            pathLength={1}
          />
        ) : showNumeral ? (
          <text
            className="cycle-ring-label"
            x={arc.centre}
            y={arc.textY}
            textAnchor="middle"
            fontSize={arc.fontSize}
          >
            {percent}%
          </text>
        ) : null}
      </svg>
    </div>
  );
}
```

(`pathLength={1}` makes the check's dash array size-independent, so one keyframe serves 72, 56 and 40. A round-capped arc at 0 % would still paint a dot at twelve o'clock, so the arc element is omitted when the fraction is 0; at 1 the dash array is `C C` and the caps meet without a seam.)

Create `app/components/instruments/CreditBar.tsx`:

```tsx
"use client";

import { creditBarLayout, type InstrumentState } from "../../lib/instruments";

export type CreditBarProps = {
  counted: number;
  required: number;
  minimum?: number;
  cap?: number;
  state: InstrumentState;
  label: string;
  valueText?: string;
  reducedMotion?: boolean;
  className?: string;
};

/*
 * A bar with no cap turns "complete" on its own once counted reaches
 * required (the hero bar, every minimum row); a maximum row keeps the state
 * its caller passes — reaching a cap is not completion — and an overflow is
 * painted in the overdue ink whatever the state.
 */
export function CreditBar({
  counted,
  required,
  minimum,
  cap,
  state,
  label,
  valueText,
  reducedMotion,
  className,
}: CreditBarProps) {
  const layout = creditBarLayout({ counted, required, minimum, cap });
  const shownState: InstrumentState =
    cap === undefined && layout.met ? "complete" : state;
  return (
    <div
      className={["instrument", "credit-bar", className]
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(" ")}
      data-state={shownState}
      data-overflow={layout.overflow ? "true" : undefined}
      data-reduced-motion={reducedMotion ? "true" : undefined}
      role="progressbar"
      aria-label={label}
      aria-valuemin={0}
      aria-valuemax={required}
      aria-valuenow={Math.min(counted, required)}
      aria-valuetext={valueText}
    >
      <span
        className="credit-bar-fill"
        style={{ width: `${layout.fillPercent}%` }}
      />
      {layout.minimumPercent !== undefined ? (
        <span
          className="credit-bar-mark"
          data-kind="minimum"
          style={{ left: `${layout.minimumPercent}%` }}
          aria-hidden="true"
        />
      ) : null}
      {layout.capPercent !== undefined ? (
        <span
          className="credit-bar-mark"
          data-kind="cap"
          style={{ left: `${layout.capPercent}%` }}
          aria-hidden="true"
        />
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Create `app/components/instruments/StatusPill.tsx`:

```tsx
"use client";

import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { STATE_LABELS, type InstrumentState } from "../../lib/instruments";

export type StatusPillProps = {
  state: InstrumentState;
  children?: ReactNode;
  compact?: boolean;
  className?: string;
};

/*
 * State in form and colour, with text: the colour comes from data-state, the
 * text is always in the DOM. The compact form is the 8px check-in dot; its
 * text is visually hidden, never absent (a11y-11).
 */
export function StatusPill({
  state,
  children,
  compact,
  className,
}: StatusPillProps) {
  const text = children ?? STATE_LABELS[state];
  return (
    <span
      className={["instrument", "status-pill", className]
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(" ")}
      data-state={state}
      data-compact={compact ? "true" : undefined}
    >
      {compact ? <span className="sr-only">{text}</span> : text}
    </span>
  );
}
```

Create `app/components/instruments/DeadlineTimeline.tsx`:

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { addMonthsIso } from "../../lib/dates";
import {
  STATE_LABELS,
  timelineLayout,
  type TimelineDeadline,
} from "../../lib/instruments";

export type DeadlineTimelineProps = {
  today: string;
  deadlines: readonly TimelineDeadline[];
  months?: number;
  formatDate: (iso: string) => string;
  formatShortDate: (iso: string) => string;
  formatMonth: (iso: string) => string;
  onSelect?: (id: string) => void;
  className?: string;
};

// The mockup's plot: 340 × 92 user units; the axis sits at y 52.
const PLOT_WIDTH = 340;
const PLOT_HEIGHT = 92;

/*
 * The SVG is decorative (axis, ticks, the dashed today line, one name and
 * short date per deadline). The list laid over it is the real content: one
 * 44px button per deadline, named "<label>, <date>, <state>", with a tooltip
 * that shows on hover and keyboard focus. `today` is the app's local date
 * (todayLocal in the reminder zone), passed down — never read here.
 */
export function DeadlineTimeline({
  today,
  deadlines,
  months = 12,
  formatDate,
  formatShortDate,
  formatMonth,
  onSelect,
  className,
}: DeadlineTimelineProps) {
  const layout = timelineLayout({
    today,
    deadlines,
    months,
    width: PLOT_WIDTH,
  });
  const tipBase = useId();
  const lastMonth = addMonthsIso(layout.start, months - 1);
  const { axis } = layout;
  return (
    <figure
      className={["instrument", "deadline-timeline", className]
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(" ")}
    >
      <div className="deadline-timeline-plot">
        <svg
          viewBox={`0 0 ${PLOT_WIDTH} ${PLOT_HEIGHT}`}
          aria-hidden="true"
          focusable="false"
        >
          <line
            className="deadline-timeline-axis"
            x1={axis.x1}
            y1={axis.y}
            x2={axis.x2}
            y2={axis.y}
          />
          {layout.ticks.map((tick, index) => {
            const tall = index === 0 || tick.end;
            return (
              <g key={`${tick.label}-${tick.x}`}>
                <line
                  className="deadline-timeline-tick"
                  x1={tick.x}
                  y1={tall ? 46 : 47}
                  x2={tick.x}
                  y2={tall ? 58 : 57}
                />
                <text
                  className="deadline-timeline-tick-label"
                  x={tick.x}
                  y={76}
                  textAnchor={tick.end ? "end" : "middle"}
                >
                  {tick.label}
                </text>
              </g>
            );
          })}
          <line
            className="deadline-timeline-today"
            x1={layout.todayX}
            y1={34}
            x2={layout.todayX}
            y2={70}
          />
          <text
            className="deadline-timeline-today-label"
            x={layout.todayX}
            y={28}
            textAnchor="middle"
          >
            today
          </text>
          {layout.markers.map((marker) => (
            <g key={marker.id}>
              <text
                className="deadline-timeline-marker-name"
                x={marker.x}
                y={16}
                textAnchor="middle"
              >
                {marker.label}
              </text>
              <text
                className="deadline-timeline-marker-date"
                x={marker.x}
                y={28}
                textAnchor="middle"
              >
                {formatShortDate(marker.date)}
              </text>
            </g>
          ))}
        </svg>
        <ul
          className="deadline-timeline-list"
          aria-label="Deadlines in the next twelve months"
        >
          {layout.markers.map((marker) => {
            const tipId = `${tipBase}-${marker.id}`;
            return (
              <li
                key={marker.id}
                className="instrument"
                data-state={marker.state}
                data-r={marker.r}
                style={{ left: `${(marker.x / PLOT_WIDTH) * 100}%` }}
              >
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className="deadline-timeline-hit"
                  aria-describedby={tipId}
                  onClick={() => onSelect?.(marker.id)}
                >
                  <span className="sr-only">
                    {marker.label}, {formatDate(marker.date)},{" "}
                    {STATE_LABELS[marker.state].toLowerCase()}
                  </span>
                </button>
                <span
                  role="tooltip"
                  id={tipId}
                  className="deadline-timeline-tip"
                >
                  {marker.label} · {formatDate(marker.date)} ·{" "}
                  {STATE_LABELS[marker.state]}
                </span>
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      </div>
      <figcaption>
        <span className="deadline-timeline-range">
          {formatMonth(layout.start)} – {formatMonth(lastMonth)}
        </span>
        {layout.beyond.length ? (
          <span className="deadline-timeline-beyond">
            {layout.beyond.map((deadline) => deadline.label).join(" and ")} sit
            beyond this window.
          </span>
        ) : null}
      </figcaption>
    </figure>
  );
}
```

```ts
// Like daysUntil: the clock read lives here, in a plain function outside any
// component body, so react-hooks/purity does not see Date.now() in render.
function credentialCountdown(credential: Credential) {

}
```

```ts
// The instrument state a pill or bar colours by (overdue / due soon / on
// track / submitted / renewed) and the ring state (credits complete wins)
// read the clock the same way, outside any component body.
function credentialInstrumentState(credential: Credential): InstrumentState {
  return stateOf(credential, Date.now());
}

function credentialRingState(credential: Credential): InstrumentState {
  return ringStateOf(credential, Date.now());
}
```

### Task 12: `EmptyState` primitive (the legacy 'L' glyph goes), `ErrorBoundary` with `resetKey`/`fallback` wrapping the routed screen, `ErrorFallback` and the not-found route on PageHeader + Button with a "Technical details" disclosure, `lantern-spin` → `spin` (spec §5.2 EmptyState/ErrorBoundary, §2 error/not-found routes; architecture-09)

**Rationale:** spec §5.2 names `EmptyState` and `ErrorBoundary` among the primitives and spec §2 row 3 lists "error/not-found routes" among what Wave 3 ships. Today three separate empty-state components live inside `app/ITrackApp.tsx` — `EmptyInline` (`:11676-11701`), `EmptyPage` (`:11703-11727`) and `EmptyModalState` (`:11754-11777`, line numbers of main @4bc32b5) — and `EmptyPage` renders the literal `L` left over from the License Lantern brand (`<span className="empty-page-mark" aria-hidden="true">L</span>` at `:11716-11718`, finding architecture-09), above a "Ready when you are" kicker nobody asked for. `app/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` has no `resetKey`/`fallback`/`reset`, so a screen that throws stays on the fallback until a full reload; `app/not-found.tsx` renders a bare `.error-fallback` section with the legacy `<h1>` and keeps the layout's default document title. The `lantern-spin` keyframe (architecture-09) is explicitly renameable — `tests/protected-identifiers.test.mjs:12-16` lists it as "Deliberately NOT pinned". This task ships one `EmptyState` (page, inline and in-sheet forms, no default mark), an `ErrorBoundary` that clears on a `resetKey` change and exposes `reset()` to a `fallback` render prop, an `ErrorFallback` and a not-found page built on `PageHeader` + `Button`/`buttonClassName` with the raw message only inside a `<details>` disclosure, and the spinner keyframe rename. a11y-12's `role` additions (the loading placeholder, `.mode-switch`, `.read-only-status`, `.credential-packet-gaps`) are Task 11's; this task adds no `aria-label` to any non-interactive element and touches none of those. Nothing in the app throws on demand, so the boundary's contract (fallback shown, raw message behind the disclosure, recovery on a `resetKey` change and on `Try again`) is proven end-to-end on the dev-only `/styleguide` samples (Task 6's route), which mount exactly the components the shell mounts; the shell wiring itself is proven by `npm run typecheck`, the `grep` in Step 6 and the whole e2e suite staying green.

**Decisions:** (1) `EmptyState` keeps an `<h2>` — `PageHeader` (Task 9) owns the page's `h1`, and `tests/e2e/credentials.spec.ts:51,75` locate `getByRole("heading", { name: "Add your first credential" })` without a level. (2) No default mark: the 'L' is deleted, not replaced; the six call sites pass `icon` only where the old component drew a plus glyph (the inline row and the three in-sheet states). (3) `app/not-found.tsx` stays OUTSIDE the app shell — vinext mounts `not-found.tsx` inside the root layout only (`node_modules/vinext/dist/server/app-page-route-wiring.js:245-249`), and the shell needs the workspace fetch — so it gets the page frame `main#main-content.app-main.app-main-solo` (Task 9's classes), a `PageHeader` with `documentTitle="Page not found · iTrack"`, no `role="alert"` (a 404 is not an alert) and a `Link` carrying `buttonClassName("primary")`. (4) `ErrorFallback` keeps `role="alert"` and its two existing sentences; the only new user-facing string is the disclosure's `Technical details`. (5) `<ErrorBoundary resetKey={buildPath(nav.route)}>` wraps the whole routed expression inside `<AppShell>` (after the banners), so the rail and bottom nav stay operable around a crashed screen and any navigation clears it. (6) `lantern-spin` becomes `spin`, which `app/styles/primitives.css` already declares for the Button spinner (Task 5); the legacy `.action-spinner` rule simply names it.

**What is on disk when this task starts (Tasks 5 and 9 have landed):** `app/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` still has the Wave 1 class (`Component<{ children: ReactNode }, …>`, no reset) but its three buttons are already `<Button>`s (Task 5 rewrote `:33-51`); `app/not-found.tsx` already reads `className="app-main app-main-solo"` on its `<main>` (Task 9) and `className={buttonClassName("primary")}` on its `Link` (Task 5) but still wraps everything in `<section className="error-fallback">` with a bare `<h1>`; `app/styles/legacy-shared.css` (Task 2) holds the verbatim legacy rules under its section banners, including `LEGACY EMPTY STATES` (`.empty-inline*`, `.empty-page*`, `.empty-modal*`) and `LEGACY ERROR FALLBACK` (`.error-fallback`, `.error-fallback h1`, `.error-fallback p`, `.error-fallback-actions`), plus `.action-spinner { … animation: lantern-spin 0.7s linear infinite; }` and `@keyframes lantern-spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }`; `app/styles/primitives.css` (Task 5, with Tasks 6–8's MODAL/FORM/TOAST sections appended) and `app/styles/shell.css` (Task 9) are consumer stylesheets (zero colour literals, no legacy alias); `app/styleguide/Styleguide.tsx` (Task 6) is a `"use client"` page whose `<main id="main-content" className="styleguide">` holds one `<section aria-labelledby>` per primitive. Both files this task rewrites whole are replaced regardless of the exact text Tasks 5 and 9 left in them.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing e2e spec `tests/e2e/error-surfaces.spec.ts`**

Five tests, all four projects. The first three run on the demo identity and save nothing; the last two write nothing either but need an account with zero credentials, so they take a fresh identity. `app.goto` resolves at once on pages without the hydration placeholder (the 404 and the styleguide).

```ts
import { expect, freshIdentity, test } from "./fixtures";

// spec §2 (Wave 3 ships the error/not-found routes) and §5.2 EmptyState /
// ErrorBoundary; architecture-09 (the legacy 'L' glyph). The 404 is served by
// the root layout outside the app shell. Nothing in the app throws on demand,
// so the boundary's contract — the fallback, the raw message only inside a
// disclosure, recovery on a resetKey change or on Try again — is proven on
// the dev-only /styleguide samples, which mount exactly the components the
// shell mounts. Runs in all four projects.

test("the 404 keeps the page frame, titles itself and links home", async ({ page, app }) => {
  await app.goto("/nonexistent");
  await expect(
    page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Page not found" }),
  ).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page).toHaveTitle("Page not found · iTrack");
  await expect(page.locator("#main-content")).toHaveCount(1);
  // A 404 is not an alert. The Toast region's assertive slot is always
  // mounted by the root layout, so the check is scoped to the page frame.
  await expect(page.locator("#main-content").getByRole("alert")).toHaveCount(0);
  await page.getByRole("link", { name: "Go to Home" }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/^https?:\/\/[^/]+\/$/);
  app.expectNoErrors();
});

test("the error fallback keeps the raw message inside a disclosure", async ({ page, app }) => {
  await app.goto("/styleguide");
  await expect(page).toHaveTitle("Styleguide · iTrack"); // hydrated before the first click (Task 6 gotcha)
  const alert = page
    .getByRole("alert")
    .filter({ hasText: "Something broke on our side" });
  await expect(alert).toBeVisible();
  await expect(
    alert.getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Something broke on our side" }),
  ).toBeVisible();
  // The message is in the DOM but closed away until the disclosure opens.
  await expect(alert.getByText("Styleguide sample error")).toBeHidden();
  await alert.getByText("Technical details").click();
  await expect(alert.getByText("Styleguide sample error")).toBeVisible();
  await expect(alert.getByRole("button", { name: "Reload" })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(alert.getByRole("button", { name: "Copy details" })).toBeVisible();
  app.expectNoErrors();
});

test("the boundary catches a render error and recovers on a reset-key change or Try again", async ({ page, app }) => {
  await app.goto("/styleguide");
  await expect(page).toHaveTitle("Styleguide · iTrack"); // hydrated before the first click (Task 6 gotcha)
  const sample = page.locator(".styleguide-boundary");
  await expect(sample.getByText("Sample screen rendered.")).toBeVisible();

  await sample.getByRole("button", { name: "Throw a sample error" }).click();
  const alert = sample.getByRole("alert");
  await expect(
    alert.getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Something broke on our side" }),
  ).toBeVisible();
  await expect(alert.getByText("Styleguide sample crash")).toBeHidden();
  await alert.getByText("Technical details").click();
  await expect(alert.getByText("Styleguide sample crash")).toBeVisible();

  // resetKey: what the shell passes as the current path; a change clears it.
  await sample.getByRole("button", { name: "Change the reset key" }).click();
  await expect(sample.getByRole("alert")).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(sample.getByText("Sample screen rendered.")).toBeVisible();

  // fallback render prop + reset(): Try again clears it on demand.
  await sample.getByRole("button", { name: "Throw a sample error" }).click();
  await expect(sample.getByRole("alert")).toBeVisible();
  await sample.getByRole("button", { name: "Try again" }).click();
  await expect(sample.getByRole("alert")).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(sample.getByText("Sample screen rendered.")).toBeVisible();
  // React reports a caught render error through console.error by design, so
  // app.expectNoErrors() is deliberately not asserted here.
});

test.describe("a new account", () => {
  test.use({ identity: freshIdentity() });

  test("the empty Credentials page is one EmptyState with no legacy glyph", async ({ page, app }) => {
    await app.goto("/credentials");
    const empty = page.locator(".empty-state");
    await expect(empty).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(
      empty.getByRole("heading", { level: 2, name: "Add your first credential" }),
    ).toBeVisible();
    // The section is named by its heading and the heading is its first text:
    // no glyph, no kicker precedes it, and a page-level state draws no mark.
    await expect(empty).toHaveAttribute("aria-labelledby", /.+/);
    await expect(empty).toHaveText(/^\s*Add your first credential/);
    await expect(empty.locator(".empty-state-mark")).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(empty.locator('[aria-hidden="true"]')).toHaveCount(0);
    await empty.getByRole("button", { name: "Set up credential" }).click();
    await expect(app.dialog("Set up a credential")).toBeVisible();
    app.expectNoErrors();
  });

  test("the Log sheet's in-sheet empty state is the compact form with a mark and a quiet action", async ({ page, app }) => {
    await app.goto("/");
    const sheet = await app.openLog();
    const empty = sheet.locator(".empty-state.empty-state-compact");
    await expect(
      empty.getByRole("heading", { level: 2, name: "Add an active credential first" }),
    ).toBeVisible();
    await expect(empty.locator(".empty-state-mark")).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(empty.locator(".empty-state-mark")).toHaveAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
    await empty.getByRole("button", { name: "Set up credential" }).click();
    await expect(sheet).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(app.dialog("Set up a credential")).toBeVisible();
    app.expectNoErrors();
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `app/components/EmptyState.tsx` and append the EMPTY STATE section to `app/styles/primitives.css`**

`app/components/EmptyState.tsx` (whole file):

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Button } from "./Button";

// One empty state for the page (Credentials, Activity log), the inline row
// (Home's recent learning) and the in-sheet case (a sheet with nothing to
// act on). No default mark: a caller that has a glyph passes `icon`; the
// section is named by its heading, which stays an h2 because PageHeader
// owns the page's h1.
export function EmptyState({
  title,
  body,
  action,
  icon,
  compact = false,
}: {
  title: string;
  body: string;
  action?: { label: string; onClick: () => void };
  icon?: ReactNode;
  compact?: boolean;
}) {
  const titleId = useId();
  return (
    <section
      className={compact ? "empty-state empty-state-compact" : "empty-state"}
      aria-labelledby={titleId}
    >
      {icon ? (
        <span className="empty-state-mark" aria-hidden="true">
          {icon}
        </span>
      ) : null}
      <div className="empty-state-text">
        <h2 id={titleId}>{title}</h2>
        <p>{body}</p>
      </div>
      {action ? (
        <Button variant={compact ? "quiet" : "primary"} onClick={action.onClick}>
          {action.label}
        </Button>
      ) : null}
    </section>
  );
}
```

Delete the 18 rules (the 17 above plus `@keyframes lantern-spin`) and their banners with a brace-matched, comment-aware pass rather than by line range — Task 2's px→rem sweep changed line counts inside these rules, so nothing here is keyed to a line number. Write the helper into the session scratchpad (it is not committed):

```bash
SCRATCH=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-chrisskerritt/9c80c811-f6db-458b-a5f8-0c60c0a9cc0a/scratchpad
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/task12"
cat > "$SCRATCH/task12/drop-legacy-rules.mjs" <<'EOF'
// Drops whole top-level CSS rules whose selector starts with one of the retired
// families, plus the comment banners that introduced them. Brace-matched and
// comment-aware, so a `{` inside a prose comment cannot desynchronise it.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const file = process.argv[2];
const DROP_RULE = /^\s*(\.empty-inline|\.empty-page|\.empty-modal|\.error-fallback|@keyframes lantern-spin)\b/;
const DROP_COMMENT = /LEGACY EMPTY STATES|LEGACY ERROR FALLBACK|Error fallback \(ErrorBoundary/;
const css = readFileSync(file, "utf8");
let out = "";
let i = 0;
let rules = 0;
let comments = 0;
while (i < css.length) {
  if (css.startsWith("/*", i)) {
    const end = css.indexOf("*/", i + 2);
    const comment = css.slice(i, end === -1 ? css.length : end + 2);
    if (DROP_COMMENT.test(comment)) comments += 1;
    else out += comment;
    i += comment.length;
    continue;
  }
  const open = css.indexOf("{", i);
  if (open === -1) {
    out += css.slice(i);
    break;
  }
  const selector = css.slice(i, open);
  const commentStart = selector.indexOf("/*");
  if (commentStart !== -1) {
    out += selector.slice(0, commentStart);
    i += commentStart;
    continue;
  }
  let depth = 0;
  let j = open;
  for (; j < css.length; j += 1) {
    if (css.startsWith("/*", j)) {
      j = css.indexOf("*/", j + 2) + 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (css[j] === "{") depth += 1;
    else if (css[j] === "}" && (depth -= 1) === 0) break;
  }
  const rule = css.slice(i, j + 1);
  if (DROP_RULE.test(selector)) rules += 1;
  else out += rule;
  i = j + 1;
}
writeFileSync(file, out.replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n"));
console.log(`dropped ${rules} rules and ${comments} comments from ${file}`);
EOF

sed -i '' 's/animation: lantern-spin 0.7s linear infinite;/animation: spin 0.7s linear infinite;/' app/styles/legacy-shared.css
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Rewrite `app/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx`, append the ERROR FALLBACK section to `app/styles/shell.css`, and wrap the routed screen in `app/ITrackApp.tsx`**

`app/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` (whole file — replaces the Wave 1 class and the Task 5 fallback):

```tsx
"use client";

import { Component, type ErrorInfo, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { describeError } from "../lib/clientError";
import { reportClientError } from "./ClientErrorBeacon";
import { Button } from "./Button";

type ErrorBoundaryState = { error: unknown | null };
type ErrorBoundaryProps = {
  children: ReactNode;
  // Changing the key (the shell passes the current path) clears a caught
  // error, so a crashed screen recovers on the next navigation.
  resetKey?: string;
  fallback?: (error: unknown, reset: () => void) => ReactNode;
};

export class ErrorBoundary extends Component<ErrorBoundaryProps, ErrorBoundaryState> {
  state: ErrorBoundaryState = { error: null };

  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: unknown): ErrorBoundaryState {
    return { error };
  }

  componentDidCatch(error: unknown, info: ErrorInfo) {
    reportClientError(error);
    console.error("iTrack render error", error, info.componentStack);
  }

  componentDidUpdate(previous: ErrorBoundaryProps) {
    if (this.state.error !== null && previous.resetKey !== this.props.resetKey) {
      this.setState({ error: null });
    }
  }

  reset = () => this.setState({ error: null });

  render() {
    if (this.state.error === null) return this.props.children;
    if (this.props.fallback) return this.props.fallback(this.state.error, this.reset);
    return <ErrorFallback error={this.state.error} onReset={this.reset} />;
  }
}

// The crash surface for the boundary, app/error.tsx and the styleguide
// sample. The raw message is rendered only inside the disclosure; the
// visible copy stays the two sentences Wave 1 shipped.
export function ErrorFallback({
  error,
  onReset,
  title = "Something broke on our side",
  body = "Your data is safe on the server. Reload to pick up where you left off.",
}: {
  error: unknown;
  onReset?: () => void;
  title?: string;
  body?: string;
}) {
  const details = describeError(error);
  const copyDetails = () => {
    const text = `${details.message}\n${details.stack}\n${window.location.href}\n${new Date().toISOString()}`;
    void window.navigator.clipboard?.writeText(text).catch(() => {});
  };
  return (
    <section className="error-fallback" role="alert">
      <h1 className="page-title">{title}</h1>
      <p>{body}</p>
      <div className="error-fallback-actions">
        <Button variant="primary" onClick={() => window.location.reload()}>
          Reload
        </Button>
        <Button variant="secondary" onClick={copyDetails}>
          Copy details
        </Button>
        {onReset ? (
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onReset}>
            Try again
          </Button>
        ) : null}
      </div>
      <details className="error-fallback-details">
        <summary>Technical details</summary>
        <pre>{details.message}</pre>
      </details>
    </section>
  );
}
```

(`new Date().toISOString()` inside the copy handler is the Wave 1 line unchanged; the `tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs` today-in-UTC guard matches only `.toISOString().slice(0, 10)` and `const todayIso`. The `resetKey` comparison lives in `componentDidUpdate`, which React's class API permits; the `react-hooks` rules do not apply to classes.)

Add at module level (above the page component; a module-level `Error` keeps `react-hooks/purity` out of the render path and makes the static fallback's disclosure identical on every visit):

```tsx
// A static error captured once at module load: the sample fallback renders
// it on every visit, so the disclosure's contents are stable for e2e and axe.
const SAMPLE_ERROR = new Error("Styleguide sample error");

function SampleScreen({ crashed }: { crashed: boolean }) {
  if (crashed) throw new Error("Styleguide sample crash");
  return <p>Sample screen rendered.</p>;
}

// The ErrorBoundary contract the shell relies on, on demand: a render error
// shows the fallback; a resetKey change (the shell passes the current path)
// clears it; the `fallback` render prop's reset() clears it from Try again.
function BoundarySample() {
  const [crashed, setCrashed] = useState(false);
  const [resetKey, setResetKey] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="styleguide-boundary">
      <p>
        <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setCrashed(true)}>
          Throw a sample error
        </Button>{" "}
        <Button
          variant="secondary"
          onClick={() => {
            setCrashed(false);
            setResetKey((key) => key + 1);
          }}
        >
          Change the reset key
        </Button>
      </p>
      <ErrorBoundary
        resetKey={String(resetKey)}
        fallback={(error, reset) => (
          <ErrorFallback
            error={error}
            onReset={() => {
              setCrashed(false);
              reset();
            }}
          />
        )}
      >
        <SampleScreen crashed={crashed} />
      </ErrorBoundary>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Task 13: The §9 gates: `@axe-core/playwright` on every route, the Log sheet, the load-failure state and the styleguide in all four projects (zero serious/critical), 320 px reflow, forced-colours proof, and the Wave 3 screenshot evidence (32 PNGs committed under `docs/design/wave3/`)

**Rationale:** spec §9 makes axe a gate from Wave 3 ("axe on every route with zero serious/critical violations"), and the §2 Wave 3 row's finish gate is "contrast audit green, both schemes, desktop + phone screenshots". The contrast audit has been green at every commit since Task 1; the four Playwright projects (Wave 2 Task 3) already cover scheme × viewport (1440×900 and 390×844, light and dark), and the mockup README's decision 5 fixes the shape of the gate: no WebKit project, axe in all four Chromium projects, zero serious/critical. `playwright.config.ts:6-8` still says "only the axe gate arrives with Wave 3" — this task is that gate, plus the two per-file variants the audit findings ask for and the finish-gate evidence as files in the repo. The findings this task proves closed rather than fixes: a11y-12 (`aria-prohibited-attr` — `aria-label` on a role-less `<div>` — is impact **serious** in axe-core 4.13.0, so the role additions of Tasks 9 and 11 are load-bearing for the gate); a11y-13 (the screen-stack bleed that made 320 px pages 322 px wide — the stack is gone with Task 9, and `tests/e2e/reflow.spec.ts` keeps it gone); a11y-M-01 (custom check rows that lost their state under Windows high contrast — Task 7's `@media (forced-colors: active)` rules for the legacy rows and Task 11's for the instruments are what `tests/e2e/forced-colors.spec.ts` exercises). `@axe-core/playwright` 4.13.0 is the one new devDependency the wave allows (Global Constraints, "package.json changes exactly three times"): it exports `AxeBuilder` by name (`export { AxeBuilder, AxeBuilder as default }`), `analyze()` returns axe-core's `AxeResults`, its only dependency is `axe-core ~4.13.0` (eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y's transitive `axe-core ^4.10.0` is satisfied by 4.13.0 too, so npm either hoists one 4.13.0 or nests it beside the locked 4.11.4 — no conflict either way) and its peer `playwright-core >= 1.0.0` is met by `@playwright/test` 1.63.0.

**Decisions.** (1) The gate is impact-based and never rule-narrowed: `.withTags`, `.disableRules` and `.exclude` are forbidden; `moderate`/`minor` violations are counted into a per-surface annotation and the full result is attached to the report, but only `serious`/`critical` are asserted — and the assertion prints rule id, impact, help text and every node's selector, so a red run names the fix. (2) One `test()` per surface (seven routes, the Log sheet, the load-failure state = nine per project, 36 in all) rather than one test looping surfaces: a failure names its surface and the other surfaces are still audited in the same run. (3) The crash fallback is covered through the styleguide's static `ErrorFallback` sample (Task 12) and the load-failure state through `page.route` returning a 500 from `/api/workspace` (the title `WorkspaceLoadFailure` renders for a status ≥ 500 is "iTrack is temporarily unavailable."); no `?__crash` hook is added to the app. (4) 32 screenshots are committed (8 surfaces × 4 projects, viewport-only, CSS pixels — the phone descriptor's 3× scale factor would otherwise write 1170×2532 PNGs); `WAVE3_SCREENSHOTS=full` captures full pages for a local look and is never committed; the capture spec is skipped unless the env var is set, so the ordinary e2e run never writes into `docs/`. The clock is fixed and the time zone pinned so the greeting and the countdowns read the same in every project. - [ ] **Step 1: Write the axe gate (the failing test)**

Create `tests/e2e/axe.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { AxeBuilder } from "@axe-core/playwright";
import type { Page } from "@playwright/test";
import { expect, test } from "./fixtures";

// spec §9: axe on every route with zero serious/critical violations, in all
// four projects (mockup README decision 5: no WebKit project, all four
// Chromium projects). One test per surface, so a failure names the surface
// and the other surfaces are still audited in the same run. The full axe
// result is attached per surface; moderate/minor counts are annotated,
// never asserted. No rule is excluded and no tag narrows the run — the
// gate is impact-based. Demo identity, read-only: the Log sheet is opened,
// never submitted.

// axe-core's types are not imported directly: the hoisted axe-core is
// eslint's 4.11, not the 4.13 nested under @axe-core/playwright.
type AxeResults = Awaited<ReturnType<AxeBuilder["analyze"]>>;

const BLOCKING = new Set(["serious", "critical"]);

async function audit(page: Page, label: string): Promise<AxeResults> {
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();
  const info = test.info();
  await info.attach(`axe-${label}`, {
    body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
    contentType: "application/json",
  });
  const counts: Record<string, number> = { minor: 0, moderate: 0, serious: 0, critical: 0 };
  for (const violation of results.violations) counts[violation.impact ?? "minor"] += 1;
  info.annotations.push({
    type: "axe",
    description: `${label} (${info.project.name}): ${JSON.stringify(counts)}`,
  });
  const blocking = results.violations.filter((violation) =>
    BLOCKING.has(violation.impact ?? ""),
  );
  expect(
    blocking.map(
      (violation) =>
        `${violation.id} [${violation.impact}] ${violation.help}\n  ${violation.nodes
          .map((node) => node.target.join(" "))
          .join("\n  ")}`,
    ),
    `${label}: serious/critical axe violations`,
  ).toEqual([]);
  return results;
}

// The demo credential's id is read from the workspace, so the detail route
// is the real one; app.goto waits for the hydration placeholder to leave,
// so axe never audits the skeleton. The 404 and the styleguide render no
// placeholder and resolve at once.
const ROUTES: ReadonlyArray<[label: string, path: string | ((id: string) => string)]> = [
  ["home", "/"],
  ["credentials", "/credentials"],
  ["credential-detail", (id) => `/credentials/${id}`],
  ["activity-log", "/history"],
  ["account", "/profile"],
  ["not-found", "/nonexistent"],
  ["styleguide", "/styleguide"],
];

for (const [label, path] of ROUTES) {
  test(`${label} passes axe with no serious or critical violations`, async ({ page, app }) => {
    const id = await app.demoCredentialId();
    await app.goto(typeof path === "function" ? path(id) : path);
    await audit(page, label);
    app.expectNoErrors();
  });
}

test("the Log activity sheet passes axe while open", async ({ page, app }) => {
  await app.goto("/");
  await app.openLog();
  await audit(page, "log-activity-sheet");
  app.expectNoErrors();
});

test("the workspace-load-failure state passes axe", async ({ page, app }) => {
  // A 500 from the workspace fetch renders WorkspaceLoadFailure in place of
  // the loading placeholder, titled for a status >= 500. Nothing reaches
  // the dev server.
  await page.route(
    (url) => url.pathname === "/api/workspace",
    (route) =>
      route.fulfill({
        status: 500,
        contentType: "application/json",
        body: JSON.stringify({ error: "boom", code: "boom" }),
      }),
  );
  await app.goto("/");
  await expect(
    page.getByRole("heading", { name: "iTrack is temporarily unavailable." }),
  ).toBeVisible();
  await audit(page, "load-failure");
});
```

Every test's annotation reads like `home (desktop-light): {"minor":0,"moderate":1,"serious":0,"critical":0}` — the moderate/minor counts are information (`region`, `landmark-one-main`, `page-has-heading-one` on the styleguide, where the static `ErrorFallback` sample carries a second `h1.page-title`, are all impact `moderate`), and each test's `axe-<surface>` attachment under `test-results/` holds the full result (`violations`, `incomplete`, `passes`) for reading.

If a test is red, its message lists `<rule id> [<impact>] <help>` and the failing nodes' selectors. Fix the markup or the token, re-run, and never reach for `.exclude(…)`, `.disableRules(…)` or `.withTags(…)` — `.exclude('[inert]')` in particular would hide a real defect. The suspects, by rule (impacts are axe-core 4.13.0's):

| Rule (impact) | Where it comes from | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `aria-prohibited-attr` (serious) | an `aria-label` on a role-less `<div>`/`<span>` (a11y-12). Task 9 dropped the brand's, Task 11 gave `.mode-switch`, `.credential-packet-gaps`, `.read-only-status` and the hydration placeholder a role. | `grep -n 'aria-label=' app/ITrackApp.tsx app/components/*.tsx app/components/instruments/*.tsx \| grep -v 'role=\|<button\|<nav\|<section\|<input\|<a \|<ul\|<label'` lists any survivor: add `role="group"` (or drop the label when visible text already names the element). |
| `color-contrast` (serious) | a legacy rule reading an alias that maps to too light an ink, or a state pair on the wrong surface. The node's `any[0].data` in the attachment carries `fgColor`, `bgColor`, `contrastRatio`, `expectedContrastRatio`; `node tools/contrast-audit.mjs --json` prints every token's resolved hex per scheme, so the pair maps back to names. | Re-point the alias in the `LEGACY ALIASES` block of `app/styles/tokens.css` (e.g. an ink alias → `--ink-muted`) or the rule's surface — never a literal in a consumer stylesheet. `node tools/contrast-audit.mjs` stays exit 0. |
| `duplicate-id-aria` (critical) / `aria-valid-attr-value` (critical) | a fixed id rendered twice (the styleguide mounts several samples of one component), or an `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` naming an id that is not in the DOM. | `useId()` in the component; make the referenced id real. |
| `scrollable-region-focusable` (serious) | a container with `overflow: auto` that overflows (the History records table wrapper at the phone widths, a `<pre>` in a disclosure) and holds no focusable child. | `tabIndex={0}` plus `role="region"` and an `aria-label` on the scroll container. |
| `nested-interactive` (serious) | a control inside a control — a `<button>` inside the `<label className="task-toggle">` that wraps a checkbox, or inside a `<summary>`. | Move the inner control out of the outer one. |
| `aria-hidden-focus` (serious) | a focusable element inside `aria-hidden="true"` — a legacy wrapper still carrying the attribute. | Remove the attribute (the shell and the Modal use `inert`, never `aria-hidden`, since Tasks 6 and 9). |
| `label` / `select-name` (critical) | a form control with no accessible name. | Wrap it in `Field` (Task 7) or give it an `aria-label`. |
| `document-title` (serious) | no `<title>` — the root layout always emits one, so this only fires if a route's metadata render broke. | Fix the layout render; do not add per-page titles by hand. |
| `landmark-unique` (moderate — annotated, not asserted) | both navs named "Primary navigation" visible at one viewport. | Not a gate failure, but it means `shell.css`'s 820 px block is not hiding the rail or the bottom nav at that width — fix it there. |

Then, once green, prove the gate bites: temporarily add `aria-label="probe"` to the `<div className="task-list">` in `app/ITrackApp.tsx` (`grep -n 'className="task-list"' app/ITrackApp.tsx`), re-run `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 npx playwright test tests/e2e/axe.spec.ts --project=desktop-light`, and expect `home passes axe …` to FAIL with `aria-prohibited-attr [serious] Elements must only use permitted ARIA attributes` naming `.task-list` (`the Log activity sheet passes axe while open` fails the same way unless axe skips the page it finds inert behind the open sheet — either result is fine); revert the probe (`git checkout -- app/ITrackApp.tsx` if it is the only change there, otherwise remove the attribute by hand) and re-run to `9 passed`.

- [ ] **Step 6: The 320 px reflow proof and the forced-colours proof**

Create `tests/e2e/reflow.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from "./fixtures";

// a11y-13 (WCAG 1.4.10): no route scrolls horizontally at 320 CSS px — the
// screen-stack bleed that made pages 322px wide is gone with the stack, and
// this keeps it gone. A per-file viewport override: the four projects
// (scheme, user agent, touch) stay as they are, so this runs 320px wide
// under both schemes with and without the phone descriptor. The measure is
// honest only while nothing hides horizontal overflow at the root, so that
// is asserted alongside it. Demo identity, read-only.
test.describe("320px reflow", () => {
  test.use({ viewport: { width: 320, height: 568 } });

  test("no route or sheet overflows the viewport", async ({ page, app }) => {
    const id = await app.demoCredentialId();
    const expectNoOverflow = async (label: string) => {
      const measured = await page.evaluate(() => ({
        excess:
          document.documentElement.scrollWidth -
          document.documentElement.clientWidth,
        rootOverflowX: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).overflowX,
        bodyOverflowX: getComputedStyle(document.body).overflowX,
      }));
      expect(measured.rootOverflowX, `${label}: html hides overflow`).not.toMatch(
        /^(hidden|clip)$/,
      );
      expect(measured.bodyOverflowX, `${label}: body hides overflow`).not.toMatch(
        /^(hidden|clip)$/,
      );
      expect(measured.excess, `${label}: horizontal overflow in CSS px`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
    };

    for (const route of [
      "/",
      "/credentials",
      `/credentials/${id}`,
      "/history",
      "/profile",
      "/nonexistent",
      "/styleguide",
    ]) {
      await app.goto(route);
      await expectNoOverflow(route);
    }

    // An open sheet locks body scrolling (Modal), so the document measure
    // stands alone here and the card is measured as well.
    await app.goto("/");
    await app.openLog();
    const sheet = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const card = document.querySelector(".modal-card");
      return {
        excess:
          document.documentElement.scrollWidth -
          document.documentElement.clientWidth,
        cardExcess: card
          ? card.scrollWidth - card.clientWidth
          : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
      };
    });
    expect(sheet.excess, "log sheet: document overflow in CSS px").toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
    expect(sheet.cardExcess, "log sheet: modal card overflow in CSS px").toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
    app.expectNoErrors();
  });
});
```

Create `tests/e2e/forced-colors.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from "./fixtures";

// a11y-M-01: under forced colours (Windows high contrast) a checked box and
// an unchecked box must still differ, no unchecked box may show a check
// glyph, and a ring's arc must still read against its track. The rules
// under test are the `@media (forced-colors: active)` blocks the legacy
// choice rows (legacy-shared.css) and the instruments (instruments.css)
// carry; emulating the media feature is what makes them apply. Demo
// identity, read-only: the requirement row toggled below lives in the Log
// sheet, which is never submitted.
test("check rows and instruments keep their state under forced colours", async ({ page, app }) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: "active" });
  await app.goto("/");

  // Home's checklist: the demo seed has three tasks, one completed.
  const boxes = page.locator(".task-row .custom-check");
  await expect(boxes.first()).toBeVisible();
  const states = await boxes.evaluateAll((elements) =>
    elements.map((element) => ({
      checked:
        element.closest(".task-row")?.classList.contains("completed") ?? false,
      background: getComputedStyle(element).backgroundColor,
      adjust: getComputedStyle(element).getPropertyValue("forced-color-adjust"),
      glyphShown: Array.from(element.querySelectorAll("svg")).some(
        (svg) => getComputedStyle(svg).display !== "none",
      ),
    })),
  );
  const checked = states.filter((state) => state.checked);
  const unchecked = states.filter((state) => !state.checked);
  expect(checked.length, "the demo seed has a completed task").toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(unchecked.length, "the demo seed has a pending task").toBeGreaterThan(0);
  for (const state of states) {
    expect(state.adjust, "the box opts out of forced-colour adjustment").toBe("none");
  }
  for (const state of unchecked) {
    expect(state.glyphShown, "an unchecked box shows no glyph").toBe(false);
  }
  for (const state of checked) {
    expect(state.glyphShown, "a checked box shows its glyph").toBe(true);
  }
  expect(checked[0].background).not.toBe(unchecked[0].background);

  // The hero instruments: the arc (Highlight) against the track
  // (ButtonFace), the fill (Highlight) against the bar (ButtonFace) — both
  // opted out of adjustment so the value is not flattened away.
  const ring = page.locator(".cycle-ring").first();
  await expect(ring).toBeVisible();
  const strokes = await ring.evaluate((element) => {
    const track = element.querySelector(".cycle-ring-track");
    const arc = element.querySelector(".cycle-ring-arc");
    return {
      track: track ? getComputedStyle(track).stroke : null,
      arc: arc ? getComputedStyle(arc).stroke : null,
      adjust: arc
        ? getComputedStyle(arc).getPropertyValue("forced-color-adjust")
        : null,
    };
  });
  expect(strokes.arc, "the demo ring is 13% counted, so it draws an arc").not.toBeNull();
  expect(strokes.adjust).toBe("none");
  expect(strokes.arc).not.toBe(strokes.track);
  const bar = page.locator(".credit-bar").first();
  await expect(bar).toBeVisible();
  const fills = await bar.evaluate((element) => {
    const fill = element.querySelector(".credit-bar-fill");
    return {
      bar: getComputedStyle(element).backgroundColor,
      fill: fill ? getComputedStyle(fill).backgroundColor : null,
    };
  });
  expect(fills.fill).not.toBeNull();
  expect(fills.fill).not.toBe(fills.bar);

  // The Log sheet's requirement rows open unchecked; clicking one row (the
  // label — its opacity-0 input sits under the backdrop's hit test) checks
  // it, and only that row shows a glyph. Guarded: a seed without taggable
  // requirements must not fail this for the wrong reason.
  const sheet = await app.openLog();
  const rows = sheet.locator("label.requirement-choice");
  if ((await rows.count()) > 0) {
    await rows.first().click();
    const choices = await rows.evaluateAll((elements) =>
      elements.map((element) => {
        const box = element.querySelector(".requirement-check");
        const input = element.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>(
          'input[type="checkbox"]',
        );
        return {
          checked: input?.checked ?? false,
          background: box ? getComputedStyle(box).backgroundColor : null,
          glyphShown: box
            ? Array.from(box.querySelectorAll("svg")).some(
                (svg) => getComputedStyle(svg).display !== "none",
              )
            : false,
        };
      }),
    );
    expect(choices[0].checked, "the clicked row is checked").toBe(true);
    expect(choices[0].glyphShown, "the checked row shows its glyph").toBe(true);
    for (const row of choices.slice(1)) {
      expect(row.glyphShown, "an unchecked row shows no glyph").toBe(false);
    }
    if (choices.length > 1) {
      expect(choices[0].background).not.toBe(choices[1].background);
    }
  }
  app.expectNoErrors();
});
```

```ts
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { expect, test } from "./fixtures";

// The spec §2 finish-gate evidence: every surface in every project, written
// under docs/design/wave3/ and committed. Off by default so the ordinary
// e2e run never writes into docs/; WAVE3_SCREENSHOTS=1 captures the
// viewport, =full the whole page (for a local look only — never committed).
// Demo identity, read-only. The clock and the time zone are fixed so the
// greeting and the countdowns read the same in all four projects; fonts are
// awaited so the shots show the shipped faces, not the metric-matched
// fallbacks; `scale: "css"` keeps the phone shots at 390×844 rather than
// the descriptor's 3×.
const OUT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../docs/design/wave3/", import.meta.url));
const FULL = process.env.WAVE3_SCREENSHOTS === "full";

test.skip(
  !process.env.WAVE3_SCREENSHOTS,
  "set WAVE3_SCREENSHOTS=1 (or =full) to capture the Wave 3 gate screenshots",
);
test.use({ timezoneId: "America/New_York" });

test("captures every surface in this project's scheme and viewport", async ({ page, app }) => {
  await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date("2026-09-15T15:00:00"));
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: "reduce" });
  const project = test.info().project.name;
  const id = await app.demoCredentialId();
  const shoot = async (slug: string, fullPage: boolean) => {
    await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready.then(() => undefined));
    await page.screenshot({
      path: path.join(OUT, `${slug}-${project}.png`),
      fullPage,
      animations: "disabled",
      scale: "css",
    });
  };
  const surfaces: ReadonlyArray<[slug: string, route: string]> = [
    ["home", "/"],
    ["credentials", "/credentials"],
    ["credential-detail", `/credentials/${id}`],
    ["activity-log", "/history"],
    ["account", "/profile"],
    ["not-found", "/nonexistent"],
    ["styleguide", "/styleguide"],
  ];
  for (const [slug, route] of surfaces) {
    await app.goto(route);
    await shoot(slug, FULL);
  }
  await app.goto("/");
  await app.openLog();
  // A fixed-position sheet is captured with the viewport, never full-page.
  await shoot("log-activity", false);
  app.expectNoErrors();
});
```

### Task 14: Docs for the ledger system: `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` rewritten (token file, palette character, state/inverse/instrument families, contrast discipline with the 1.10/1.09 elevation note, the three faces, the rem scale, the three motion moments, the alias ban, the gates), the contrast-audit header prose, README useful checks, and the spec's §5.1 type paragraph amended to the shipped faces

**Rationale:** spec §5.1 is the identity as a design brief and §5.2 ends with the file layout ("Tokens in `app/styles/tokens.css`; per-screen styles in `app/styles/<screen>.css`; `globals.css` shrinks to resets + tokens import"); §9 names the gates. `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` at main `4bc32b5` describes the system all of that replaced — `app/globals.css` as the token file "today" with `tokens.css` "after the Wave 3 split" (`:3-4`), the system grey/blue character (`:17-27`), 142 light / 122 dark tokens (`:31-32`), 98 claims (`:93`), a 1.15:1 dark-elevation rule (`:105-107`), `--font-ui` and a px scale with a 10px tab-label exception (`:130-141`), press/screen/sheet motion (`:150-165`), the old theme colours (`:171`) and a forced-colors block that no longer exists in that shape (`:184-188`) — and Wave 4's screen writers read this file first. Four findings land here rather than in code: architecture-11 asked that the design-system doc describe the split layout the wave adopted ("the contrast audit assumes one file"); a11y-14 wants the rem scale stated as the rule, with the 10px exception gone (this wave retires it — the bottom-nav label is `--text-2xs` on a 22px icon); perf-08 wants the font budget and the self-hosting constraint written down; ios-coupling-09 wants the Typography section to state the actual constraint (no render-blocking font) and drop the Capacitor rationale. The spec's `- **Type:**` bullet still promises "Bricolage Grotesque (Google Fonts, variable; 600–800 … optical size for numerals ≥ 32 px)" and "IBM Plex Mono"; Task 4 shipped static 700/800 instances with `opsz` pinned at 96 (a live optical-size axis alone exceeds the 40 kB budget) and renamed the Plex subset "iTrack Mono" for its Reserved Font Name — the spec records that in one amended sentence and nothing else. `tools/contrast-audit.mjs`'s header still describes token blocks by the example of `globals.css`'s responsive `:root` (`:28-30`), which Task 1 deleted; the prose is brought to the split (Task 3 already removed its Tailwind sentence; the code is untouched). `README.md`'s "Useful checks" gains the six checks a person runs by hand — the font build, the audit, the styleguide, the screenshots, the run-check, the Playwright live smoke — so nobody has to open the plan to find them.

**Decisions taken here (binding for this task):**

1. The doc quotes only numbers a tool prints or a listing shows — the audit's claim count and stylesheet count, the per-block declaration counts of `tokens.css`, the seven woff2 byte sizes — and a scratch doc-contract check (Step 2) re-derives every one of them. When tool and doc disagree the doc is corrected, never the tool or the token file. The values written below are the ones Tasks 1 and 4 expected (85 claims = 43 light + 42 dark; 18 stylesheets; 71 / 39 / 112 declarations; 25,848 / 25,244 / 11,056 / 11,156 / 11,912 / 10,520 / 10,516 bytes — Task 4 Step 4's pinned build output, byte-reproducible); Step 1 records what the tree actually prints and Step 8 refuses to pass until the doc matches it.
2. Font file names are written as `<name>-<hash8>.woff2`: the eight-hex content hash changes on every rebuild, and `app/lib/fonts.ts` is the manifest. Byte sizes are quoted verbatim.
3. No retired name appears as a token: `--ink-surface`, `--on-dark`, `--accent-bright`, `--font-ui` are not written anywhere in the doc (the alias family is described in words; the audit's dormant 1.15 elevation floor is described by its `ink-surface` prefix without the dashes). No sentence mentions Capacitor, `next/font` as an option, or a 10px exception as current.
4. Every token in `tokens.css` is accounted for, and the doc says which task consumes it: `--duration-complete` (320 ms) is the check drawing in `instruments.css` (Task 11 keys the arc and the check's delay to `--duration-fill` and the check's own duration to `--duration-complete` — no duration literal outside `tokens.css`), and `--ledger-aside-width` (380 px) is declared for Wave 4's Home ledger and documented as such. No token is described as unconsumed, and no `--topbar-height` exists (the phone app bar is `PageHeader`, sized by its content). The doc is the Wave 4 writer's map, so it says what is.
5. The audit-tool edit is anchored on the ` * WHICH FILES.` and ` *   node tools/contrast-audit.mjs ` markers, not on line numbers: Task 3 re-wrapped the paragraph between them.
6. The README subsection closes `## Local development` (after the `Node.js \`>=22.13.0\` is required.` line), so the migration paragraph does not fall under a `### Design system` heading.
7. The doc-contract check lives in the session scratchpad and is never committed: it reads `app/styles/tokens.css` and `instruments.css` as text, which `tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs` ("no test file reads client source text") forbids for anything under `tests/`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` (whole file — the main `4bc32b5` text is replaced; no earlier Wave 3 task touches it)

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the doc-contract check (the failing test) in the scratchpad**

It is a `node:test` file that holds the four documents to the tree: the audit's own numbers, every token name the doc uses, the retired names, the font sizes on disk, and the three smaller edits. Run from the worktree root (it reads relative to `process.cwd()`).

```bash
cat > "$SCRATCH/design-system-doc-check.test.mjs" <<'CHECK_MJS'
// Task 14 doc-contract check — scratch only, never committed (it reads
// stylesheets as text, which tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs forbids for
// anything under tests/). Run from the worktree root:
//   node --test "$SCRATCH/design-system-doc-check.test.mjs"
import test from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";

const root = process.cwd();
const read = (rel) => readFileSync(path.join(root, rel), "utf8");
const doc = read("docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md");
const tokens = read("app/styles/tokens.css");
const instruments = read("app/styles/instruments.css");
const tool = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(root, "tools/contrast-audit.mjs")).href);

const audit = spawnSync(process.execPath, ["tools/contrast-audit.mjs"], { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8" });
const claimLine = /^contrast-audit: app\/styles\/tokens\.css — (\d+) claims, 0 failing, 0 literals$/m.exec(audit.stdout);
const summaryLine = /^contrast-audit: (\d+) stylesheets, 0 failing claims, 0 colour literals outside token blocks$/m.exec(audit.stdout);

// Declarations per block of tokens.css — the same walk as Step 1's awk.
function blockCounts(css) {
  const counts = { light: 0, dark: 0, motion: 0, alias: 0 };
  let block = null;
  for (const line of css.split("\n")) {
    if (line.includes("LEGACY ALIASES")) block = "alias";
    else if (line.startsWith("@media (prefers-reduced-motion")) block = "motion";
    else if (line.startsWith("@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)")) block = "dark";
    else if (line.startsWith(":root {") && block === null) block = "light";
    if (block && /^\s*--[a-z0-9-]+:/.test(line)) counts[block] += 1;
  }
  return counts;
}

// `--flag` words in the doc that are CLI options, not tokens.
const CLI_FLAGS = new Set(["--list", "--json", "--test", "--port", "--project", "--experimental-sqlite", "--update-snapshots", "--save-dev", "--save-exact"]);
// Element-scoped properties instruments.css sets on .instrument[data-state]; not tokens.
const INSTRUMENT_SCOPED = new Set(["--state-ink", "--state-soft"]);

test("the doc names the one token file and quotes the audit's own numbers", () => {
  assert.equal(audit.status, 0, audit.stdout + audit.stderr);
  assert.ok(claimLine && summaryLine, audit.stdout);
  assert.match(doc, /app\/styles\/tokens\.css/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(doc, /after the Wave 3 split|`app\/globals\.css` today/);
  assert.ok(doc.includes(`${claimLine[1]} today`), `the doc quotes ${claimLine[1]} claims`);
  assert.ok(doc.includes(`${summaryLine[1]} stylesheets today`), `the doc quotes ${summaryLine[1]} stylesheets`);
  const sheet = tool.collectStylesheets(root).find((s) => s.path === "app/styles/tokens.css");
  const claims = tool.auditStylesheet(sheet.css, sheet).claims;
  const light = claims.filter((c) => c.scheme === "light").length;
  const dark = claims.filter((c) => c.scheme === "dark").length;
  assert.ok(doc.includes(`${light} in the light block, ${dark} in dark`), `the doc quotes the ${light}/${dark} claim split`);
  const counts = blockCounts(tokens);
  assert.ok(doc.includes(`${counts.light} first-class names`), `the doc quotes ${counts.light} light declarations`);
  assert.ok(doc.includes(`${counts.dark} colour tokens`), `the doc quotes ${counts.dark} dark declarations`);
  assert.ok(doc.includes(`(${counts.alias} of them)`), `the doc quotes ${counts.alias} aliases`);
  assert.doesNotMatch(doc, /\b142 tokens|\b122 restated|98 today/);
});

test("every token the doc names exists in tokens.css (the two instrument-scoped properties in instruments.css)", () => {
  const missing = [];
  for (const name of new Set(doc.match(/--[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*/g) ?? [])) {
    if (CLI_FLAGS.has(name)) continue;
    if (!(INSTRUMENT_SCOPED.has(name) ? instruments : tokens).includes(name)) missing.push(name);
  }
  assert.deepEqual(missing, []);
});

test("the doc carries no retired token, rationale or number", () => {
  assert.doesNotMatch(doc, /--ink-surface|--on-dark|--accent-bright|--font-ui|Capacitor|Google Fonts, variable|press-scale|screen-push|sheet-up/);
  assert.match(doc, /`--text-control: 16px`/);
});

test("the font table names the seven faces and quotes their sizes from public/fonts", () => {
  const files = readdirSync(path.join(root, "public/fonts")).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".woff2")).sort();
  assert.equal(files.length, 7, files.join(" "));
  for (const file of files) {
    const stem = file.replace(/-[0-9a-f]{8}\.woff2$/, "");
    assert.notEqual(stem, file, `${file} carries an 8-hex content hash`);
    assert.ok(doc.includes(`${stem}-<hash8>.woff2`), `${stem}-<hash8>.woff2 is named`);
    const bytes = statSync(path.join(root, "public/fonts", file)).size.toLocaleString("en-US");
    assert.ok(doc.includes(`${bytes} B`), `${file} is ${bytes} B; the doc must quote it`);
  }
});

test("README, the audit header and the spec's type sentence are amended", () => {
  const readme = read("README.md");
  assert.match(readme, /^### Design system$/m);
  assert.match(readme, /deploy\/railway\/runcheck\.sh/);
  assert.match(readme, /playwright\.live\.config\.ts/);
  assert.match(readme, /tools\/fonts\/build-fonts\.sh/);
  assert.match(readme, /\/styleguide/);
  const header = read("tools/contrast-audit.mjs").split("\nimport ")[0];
  assert.doesNotMatch(header, /tailwind|after the Wave 3 split|max-width: 1040px|Today app\/globals\.css/i);
  assert.match(header, /app\/styles\/tokens\.css/);
  assert.match(header, /legacy-shared\.css/);
  assert.match(header, /LEGACY ALIASES/);
  const spec = read("docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-itrack-web-redesign-design.md");
  assert.match(spec, /static 700\/800 instances with the optical-size axis pinned at 96/);
  assert.match(spec, /shipped as "iTrack Mono"/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(spec, /Google Fonts, variable/);
});
CHECK_MJS
```
